features.details: With -g, bunfig is loaded only from --config if given, otherwise from the user's global bunfig ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml or $HOME/.bunfig.toml); project bunfig keys globalDir/globalBinDir are ignored. Directory is mkdir -p'd and the process fchdir's into it; it keeps its own package.json (created as `{"dependencies": {}}` if missing). `link`/`unlink` force global=false; `prune -g` is an error.

features.name: Positional dependency spec parsing (UpdateRequest::parse)
features.details: Each positional is trimmed of space/\n/\r/\t, `\\\\` replaced by `/`, platform separators converted to posix. If not a tarball and a valid npm package name => name with empty version (bare name parses as an empty DistTag, i.e. 'latest'). Else split at first '@' after index 0: if the prefix is a valid npm name it's the alias, rest is version (`name@ver`, `alias@npm:real@ver`, `name@github:..`, `name@file:..`, `name@https://...tgz`). Otherwise whole string parsed as a spec without name (git URLs, github:, ./path, tarball URL). scp-style `user@host:path` re-parsed as git if alias had no '/'. Unparseable or nameless npm alias => `error: unrecognised dependency format: <arg>` and crash. Duplicates (same name hash and name length) dropped. For link/unlink, `x` becomes `x@link:x`.

features.name: bun add / remove: no package specified
features.details: `bun add` or `bun remove` with no package: `error: no package specified to add|remove`, then prints help, exits 0. Missing package.json: add/install (without --filter) creates `package.json` containing `{"dependencies": {}}` and retries; update -> `No package.json, so nothing to update` crash; remove -> `No package.json, so nothing to remove` crash. Empty package.json file is accepted for add/link only; otherwise exit_on_empty_package_json.

features.name: bun add: which dependency group gets written
features.details: Target list = --dev/--optional/--peer or dependencies. Without a group flag: if package.json already lists the name in another non-peer group, that existing entry is updated in place (scan stops at first group with the name in order dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies). If the name is in two or more of dependencies/devDependencies/optionalDependencies, all of them get the new spec, unless the install skips one of those groups (e.g. --omit=dev / --production) in which case only the chosen entry is rewritten. A peer entry and a non-peer entry with the same name never replace each other. With a group flag (--dev/--optional/--peer/--save-prod): entry moves to the named group (removed from other lists via fate_of_declared: list==target -> takes spec; peer entries stay; when target is peer, the devDependencies entry is kept and follows the peer's range; others removed). Empty object lists are deleted from package.json after removal. --only-missing: requests already present in any list are dropped (no rewrite).

features.name: Version literal written by bun add (caret/exact)
features.details: Two-phase: before install the entry is written as the requested literal (bare name -> `latest`); after resolution it is replaced. For npm resolution: if request was a dist-tag (incl. bare name), or `foo@npm:bar` with no version, or (--exact / update) and the request was a non-exact npm range: writes `^<resolved>` (or `<resolved>` with --exact / install.exact), keeping `npm:<name>@` alias prefix. An explicit range or exact version (`zod@^3.0.0`, `zod@3.20.0`) is written as typed. Workspace resolution -> keeps `workspace:` literal, keeps an `npm:` alias, else writes `workspace:*`. Other resolutions (git, github, tarball URL, folder, link) are written verbatim as typed. Unresolved request keeps the requested literal. For git/tarball/folder positionals without alias, the key is the resolved package name and an older entry for that name with a different literal is dropped (no duplicate keys); re-running with same URL matches existing value instead of appending. `bun add ./a-v1 ./a-v2` resolving to the same name: `error: "a" and "b" both resolve to "name"` + note `add only one of them`.

features.name: Key ordering, indentation and trailing newline preservation
features.details: When a dependency list receives new keys (remaining != 0), its properties are alphabetized (only if >1 entries). A new dependency list object is appended at the end of the root object. Existing keys edited in place keep their position. trustedDependencies additions are appended then the array is alphabetized; a new trustedDependencies array is appended at the root end. New catalog entries are appended then the catalog object alphabetized. Printing uses the cached entry's indentation, guessed from the original file (guess_indentation: tabs or N spaces), and appends a trailing newline only if the original file ended with '\n'. After editing, the printed text is re-parsed so the cache stays consistent. A file is written only if the new bytes differ from disk and from a no-op reprint of the on-disk file. Write errors: `failed to write package.json: ERR` / `... for workspace 'name': ERR` and exit 1. Parse/read errors: `failed to parse|read package.json "path": ERR` crash.

features.name: Write ordering (bun.lock then package.json)
features.details: Phase 0 (add): fold resolved positionals (lockfile rows). Phase 1 edit_after_resolve: write resolved versions into in-memory package.json ASTs and sync lockfile rows/overrides/catalogs so the next install sees no diff. bun.lock saved. Phase 2 flush (after lockfile save): add trustedDependencies learned via --trust, then write changed files. If any update request failed, exit 1 before flushing. Nothing is written when Do::WRITE_PACKAGE_JSON is off (--no-save, --dry-run).

features.name: --trust
features.details: Adds the named packages to trustedDependencies of the package.json receiving requests (deduplicated against existing, alphabetized) and installs them with lifecycle scripts allowed. Incompatible with --production and --frozen-lockfile.

features.name: --analyze / -a
features.details: Bundles the files passed as positionals with Bun's bundler, collects imported bare package names, and runs `bun add`/`bun install` with those as positionals (ONLY_MISSING enabled: only adds missing deps). Then exits 0.

features.name: Local path respelling
features.details: Folder/local tarball/link: positionals are resolved from the invoking cwd and rewritten relative to the package.json they are added to (prefix `./` unless it starts with `..`; `file:`/`link:` prefix kept; posix separators; trailing `/` kept to distinguish dir `lib.tgz/` from tarball). With -g, absolute path written. Overlong paths: `Dependency "x" has an unsafe folder path`. With --filter, one spelling per target; if spellings differ across targets: `"x" is spelled differently relative to each selected workspace; add it to one workspace at a time`.

features.name: --catalog / --catalog=NAME
features.details: Requires root package.json `workspaces` field (`--catalog requires a "workspaces" field in the root package.json`). Writes version into root catalog (`workspaces.catalog` or `catalog` at root; named -> `catalogs.<name>`; `catalogs.default` equivalent to default) and `"catalog:"`/`"catalog:<name>"` into the target. Container chosen: workspaces object if it already has catalog(s), else root if root has catalogs or workspaces is an array. Existing catalog entry reused unless explicit version given (replaces entry; note `catalog entry X changed from "a" to "b" (also used by p1, p2)`; if new exact version is within old range it is Moved back after install). Without version, an existing range in the target package.json is cataloged verbatim (npm/dist-tag/git/github/remote tarball). Existing `catalog:<g>` reference keeps its catalog. Dist-tag seeds replaced after install with `^<resolved>` (or exact with --exact; with --exact an explicit range is also replaced by the exact version); `npm:` alias preserved. Notes: `X in T now follows the catalog entry "e" instead of "d"`, `X in T keeps "d" because the catalog entry is "e"`. Errors: local paths (`--catalog cannot add "x": a local path in the catalog would resolve from the workspace root...`), workspace: specs, names equal to the root or a workspace member, declared-twice nameless positionals (`--catalog cannot add "lit": T already declares name\n  bun add name@lit --catalog=g`), combined with --global. New catalog entries alphabetized. Even without the flag, `bun add react` (no version) writes `"catalog:"` if the default catalog already lists react (auto_use); an explicit version equal to the entry also auto-uses.

features.name: add/remove/update --filter and update -r (multi-workspace edits)
features.details: add/remove: root is selected only when named explicitly (RootSelection::ExplicitOnly), `*` matches all members but not root. update/install/outdated: root selected implicitly. Patterns via workspace_selection (names, paths, `!` exclude, relational patterns like `...^ui`). No match: error (crash, silent if --silent) and nothing written; unmatched positive patterns warned. Each selected package.json is edited; bun.lock updated for the whole repo but only selected workspaces are linked into node_modules. remove --filter: workspaces that don't list the package are untouched; if none changed prints `\n<names> is not a dependency|are not dependencies of <workspaces> [time]` and exits 0. Summary printed from the perspective of the target that received all requests (or first). --global with --filter/--recursive: `--filter|--recursive cannot be used with --global`.

features.name: bun remove behavior
features.details: Removes the name from all four groups (dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies); deletes a group object that becomes empty. Errors: root not an object `package.json is not an Object {}, so there's nothing to remove!` crash; empty object `package.json is empty {}, so there's nothing to remove!` crash; no dependency groups at all `package.json doesn't have dependencies, there's nothing to remove!` exit 0. If nothing changed (name not listed) and package.json writes enabled, exit with any_failed_to_install code after install. Afterwards deletes leftover top-level `node_modules/<name>` folders whose name no longer resolves (not following an `@scope` symlink; nested copies kept), prunes dangling `.bin` links; with -g prunes global bins and relinks freed bin names. `--save-*` foreign flags ignored. Summary: prints `- <name>` rows when nothing installed, then `<N> package(s) removed [time]` counting requests that left bun.lock.

features.name: Leftover node_modules cleanup after add with skipped group
features.details: `bun add -d x --production` (or group otherwise not installed): after install, removes the top-level node_modules folder of requested names that weren't placed, then prunes bins.

features.name: bun update (no args): rewrite rules
features.details: Updates every dependency (direct and transitive) to the newest version within declared ranges, rewrites package.json of the cwd workspace and bun.lock. Never reads the manifest cache. Rewrite rule (updated_version_literal / keeps_declared_range): only `^x...`, `~x...` and exact `x.y.z` (optionally `=`/`v` prefixed, optional prerelease/build) are rewritten; ranges with spaces, `|`, `<`, `>` and other forms (`*`, `1.x`, `>=1.0.0`, dist-tags) are kept. Short ranges `~1`, `^0`, `^0.0` that rely on omitted components are kept (would narrow). Exact pins are NOT moved by plain update (only lockfile? no: exact pin keeps its version unless --latest). Operator preserved by which_version_is_pinned: Patch-pinned -> exact (or `=` prefix kept), Minor -> `~`, Major -> `^`. --exact/install.exact writes bare version, except never for peerDependencies or catalog entries used by a `catalog:` peer. `catalog:` references never rewritten; root catalog entry updated instead (entries no catalog: dependency uses stay). Only first group naming a package is rewritten, order optional, dev, dependencies, peer. npm: alias prefix kept. Workspace-linked ranges untouched. Summary note `up to date, package.json synced` when only package.json changed.

features.name: bun update <names|patterns>
features.details: `bun update <pkg>` updates pkg everywhere in bun.lock (incl. transitive) and leaves everything else; never adds a name not declared in package.json (only lockfile moves). `name@range` moves the package.json entry to newest matching (e.g. jquery@3). Dist-tag literals kept unless --latest. `catalog:` reference kept. Only registry (npm) entries rewritten. Aliased entries `<key>: npm:<name>@...` move too. A name not in bun.lock is an error. Patterns: an arg containing `*` or starting with `!` is a glob; `!` negates (multiple `!` toggle); expanded against lockfile names and aliases into concrete names (sorted). Errors: version with pattern `a version cannot be combined with a pattern: x`; version with selectors `a version cannot be combined with --dev, --prod, --no-optional or --depth 0: x`; unmatched pattern `no packages in bun.lock match "p"` / `no dependencies in the selected groups match "p"` / `no direct dependencies match "p"` exit 1; no lockfile `no bun.lock to match <subject> against` + `    bun install` exit 1. Nothing matched: `\nChecked N dependenc(y|ies), none [selected by --dev ...] [match "p"] (no changes) [time]` exit 0. Combined with -r/--filter: edits every selected workspace's package.json.

features.name: --latest / -L
features.details: Updates direct dependencies to the `latest` dist-tag regardless of range, rewriting package.json with the same range style on the new version; also rewrites exact pins, dist-tags and other ranges. Transitive deps still respect dependents' ranges. Doesn't downgrade a dep already ahead of latest (prerelease). For peerDependencies, a range that already allows the resolved version is left alone (bare update). Catalog entries steered to latest (except entries only used via overrides). Overrides-set packages stay. Error: `--latest cannot be combined with a version: <arg>` crash. Moves patchedDependencies versions.

features.name: --dev / --prod / --no-optional selectors
features.details: selects(groups, behavior): --no-optional excludes optional entries; if neither --dev nor --prod: all (peer entries included only when no selector given); --dev selects dev; --prod selects dependencies+optionalDependencies. Only select what is updated; install still installs everything (update's --production does not omit dev). Combine with names/patterns/--latest/--interactive.

features.name: --depth 0
features.details: Only root/workspace (direct) entries re-resolved; transitive deps keep locked versions unless the updated direct dep declares a range the locked version no longer satisfies. Combines with names, patterns, selectors, --latest, --recursive, --filter. Sets Do::UPDATE_DIRECT_ONLY.

features.name: --recursive / --filter for update
features.details: Without them, update only rewrites the package.json of the cwd workspace (but from root still updates transitive deps of all workspaces). -r updates every workspace's package.json; --filter only matching (and links only selected). Bare `bun update -r/--filter` loads lockfile (`nothing to update` if absent), selects lockfile workspaces, and edits each target in two passes (record originals, then write). Root catalogs edited when targeted. With -g, recursive is ignored.

features.name: Held-back rules and warnings
features.details: Never widens ranges; overrides-set packages stay; transitive deps sharing the copy of a direct entry move with it; no extra copies for a covered version; patched versions stay while range allows, reported `kept name@version (patched, v1.2.3 available)`; failed registry fetch for a transitive keeps lock + warning, for a direct dep is an error; optional git/github/tarball deps whose source can't be fetched keep lock with `warn: name@version was not checked for updates` (exit 1 and no write if explicitly named or selected by --prod/--depth 0). `bun update -g [names]` updates global packages. --no-save updates node_modules only. --dry-run prints no summary for update.

features.name: bun update --interactive (-i)
features.details: Requires stdin TTY (else `error: bun update --interactive requires an interactive terminal.` + note suggesting bun update / bun outdated, exit 1; env BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_INTERNAL_INTERACTIVE_ASSUME_TTY bypasses). Missing package.json: `missing package.json, nothing to update` + `failed to initialize bun install: ERR`. Loads lockfile (`nothing to update`), selects workspaces via --filter/-r else cwd workspace, populates manifest cache (fetch failures fatal). Lists outdated direct deps (selected by --dev/--prod/--no-optional): Current, Target (newest in range, or latest if range exhausted), Latest (respecting minimumReleaseAge). Nothing outdated: `\nChecked N dependenc(y|ies), nothing to update [time]` or `none selected by --dev ... (no changes)`. Rows grouped by type order dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, optionalDependencies, then name, then catalog name; catalog deps grouped one row each with workspace list. Header `? Select packages to update - Space to toggle, Enter to confirm, a to select all, n to select none, i to invert, l to toggle latest` (help truncated to width). Section headers with column headers Current/Target/Latest(/Workspace when any workspace name and terminal >=100 cols). Checkbox ■/□ colored red (major; minor when 0.x; patch when 0.0.x), yellow (minor), green; cursor `❯`; name hyperlinks to npmjs.org when default registry; suffix dev/peer/optional; selected target underlined; versions colored by diff. Column caps by terminal width (<60:12/7, <80:20/10, <120:35/15/15, <160:45/20/20). Viewport scrolling with `↑ N more packages above`/below; mouse wheel (SGR 1006) scrolls; hides cursor. Keys: Space toggle (if nothing in range, selects latest), a/A all, n/N none, i/I invert, l/L toggle latest for cursor row (selects it) or all selected right after 'a', j/k and arrows move (wrap), right arrow = latest, left arrow = target (both select), PageUp/PageDown, Enter or EOF confirm (`✓ Selected N package(s) to update`), Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D cancel (`x Cancelled`, exit 0). No selection: `! No packages selected for update`. --dry-run prints sorted `↑ name from → to` rows (`^`/`->` without color) and `N package(s) would be updated [time]`. Otherwise prints `Installing updates...`, rewrites package.json entries with chosen_version_literal (preserving range style; latest selection rewrites like --latest) and catalog definitions in root, then runs install as `bun update <selected...>` with --latest cleared; timer restarts.

features.name: bun outdated table
features.details: Loads lockfile (`nothing outdated` if none); missing package.json: `missing package.json, nothing outdated` + `failed to initialize bun install: ERR` crash. Workspaces: --filter/-r select (Workspace column shown), else cwd workspace. Only npm-resolved declared rows. Row listed when update version != current OR latest newer than current (is_outdated). Columns Package | Current | Update | Latest [| Workspace]; boxed table with blue borders when ANSI (`┌─┬┐` style), markdown-like `|` table otherwise; separator line before each row; padding 1 each side. Package cell: `alias@npm:real` for aliases (alias then dim `@npm:`), dim suffix ` (dev)`, ` (peer)`, ` (optional)`. Rows ordered by group: prod, dev, peer, optional (optional peer printed once under peer). Update/Latest versions colored by semver diff vs current; Latest older than current printed dim; missing update shows dim current. ` *` (blue) when minimum release age filtered the true latest, with footer `Note: The * indicates that version isn't true latest due to minimum release age`. Catalog deps grouped into one row per (name, catalog, behavior) at first workspace, Workspace cell `catalog (ws1, ws2)` or `catalog:<name> (ws...)`, forcing Workspace column. Names escaped for control chars, width via visible width. Positional patterns: glob per name and alias; `*`/`**` = all; `!*`/`!**` = nothing listed; negations exclude; with several patterns any positive match selects. Fetch failures printed after table and crash. Nothing outdated prints nothing beyond header.

features.name: Install summary format
features.details: Printed when Do::SUMMARY. Starts with a newline. For add/update requests: `installed <name>[@npm:<real>]@<version>` + ` with binaries:` and `  - <bin>` lines, or `skipped <name>@<ver> (unsupported platform)`; blank line after. New direct installs: `+ <name>@<version>` (green +), with ` (v<x> available)` when a newer version is in cache. Updated: `↑ <name> <from> → <to>` (cyan; no-color `^ name from -> to`) with optional ` (v<x> available)`. Verbose: prints sections per workspace. Dry run without install: lists ` <name>@<version>` of every reachable package. Final line: `<N> package(s) installed [time]` (for add, N = max(success, #requests)); then `Removed: N` if any; or `<N> package(s) removed [time]`; or no-op `Checked N install(s) across M package(s) (no changes|up to date, package.json synced) [time]` or `Done! Checked N package(s) (no changes) [time]` when all packages skipped; failures `Failed to install N package(s)`. Time format `[12.34ms]` for <=1500ms else `[1.23s]`. Blocked lifecycle scripts: `\n\nBlocked N postinstall(s). Run \`bun pm [-g ]untrusted\` for details.`. Fallback `[time] done`. Progress shows `Resolving dependencies` / `Resolved, downloaded and extracted [N]`; `Saved lockfile` in verbose.

features.name: --production / --frozen-lockfile / bun ci
features.details: --production: no devDependencies for local packages, implies FROZEN_LOCKFILE and FAIL_EARLY, lockfile not saved. --frozen-lockfile: lockfile not saved; errors if package.json disagrees with bun.lock (names first changed dep); edits that keep locked versions pass. No lockfile + frozen: installs without writing one. Migrated foreign lockfiles migrated in memory only.

features.name: --dry-run, --no-save, --lockfile-only, --yarn, --save-text-lockfile, --force, --no-cache
features.details: --dry-run: resolves and lists packages, no node_modules, no package.json/bun.lock/yarn.lock write, no lifecycle scripts. --no-save: no lockfile and no package.json write (link/unlink default no-save, --save opt-in). --lockfile-only: resolve and write lockfile without installing, no tarball prefetch. -y/--yarn: also write yarn.lock v1. --save-text-lockfile: text bun.lock. -f/--force: ignore manifest cache-control, reinstall all, force-save lockfile. --no-cache: skip manifest cache for this run.

features.name: --backend
features.details: Values: clonefile (macOS default), clonefile_each_dir (macOS), hardlink (Linux/Windows default), copyfile (fallback), symlink. Unknown or unsupported values silently ignored; stored in a global atomic.

features.name: --omit, --linker, --cpu/--os/--libc, --offline, --prefer-offline, --minimum-release-age
features.details: --omit dev (local dev off), optional (local+remote optional off), peer (local+remote peer off); repeatable. --linker isolated|hoisted (default Auto via configVersion/workspaces). --cpu/--os/--libc override platform filtering for optional deps. --offline never uses network; --prefer-offline uses cached manifests of any age. --minimum-release-age seconds or unit string; excludes list entries `name` or `name@exact || exact`.

areas.notes:
I read the actual sources for every area: CommandLineArguments.rs (all of it), PackageManagerOptions.rs (all of it), UpdateRequest.rs, PackageJSONEditor.rs, updatePackageJSONAndInstall.rs, add_catalog.rs, add_remove_with_filter.rs, package_json_write_back.rs, WorkspacePackageJSONCache.rs, update_scope.rs, the summary printer (install_with_manager.rs plus lockfile/printer/tree_printer.rs), and the runtime CLI files install/add/remove/update/update_interactive/outdated plus pm_update_package_json.rs. I also read all five docs pages.

Not covered in depth:
- The resolver internals of update_transitive.rs (which transitive deps get held back). Only the user-visible rules are listed, taken from update.mdx.
- workspace_selection.rs (the `--filter` pattern grammar, including relational `...^ui`).
- The flag names in the IGNORED_FOREIGN_FLAGS entry are a sample. The full list is at CommandLineArguments.rs:446-498 and should be copied verbatim.

Things worth knowing before porting:
- `bun i -g` and `bun install --global` route to AddCommand.
- `bun ci` is install plus frozen lockfile.
- For `update`, `--production` only picks which entries to update. It does not freeze the lockfile or skip devDependencies.
- `bun add` without a group flag writes to every non-peer group that lists the package. With a group flag it moves the entry.
- package.json is written after bun.lock, and only when the bytes would change.
- Indentation is guessed from the original file, and a trailing newline is kept only if the original had one.

features.name: Shared PM flag table and per-command param tables
features.details: SHARED_PARAMS (all PM commands): -c/--config <STR>? (bunfig path), -y/--yarn, -p/--production, -P/--prod, --no-save, --save, --ca <STR>..., --cafile <STR>, --dry-run, --frozen-lockfile, -f/--force, --cache-dir <PATH>, --no-cache, --silent, --quiet (only tarball name when packing), --verbose, --no-progress, --no-summary, --no-verify, --offline, --prefer-offline, --ignore-scripts, --trust, -g/--global, --cwd <STR>, --env-file <STR>..., --no-env-file, --backend <STR> (macOS default clonefile; else hardlink; values clonefile|hardlink|symlink|copyfile; unsupported value silently ignored), --registry <STR> (must start with http:// or https:// else crash; error redacts creds), --concurrent-scripts <NUM> (0 => default 2x cores; invalid ignored), --network-concurrency <NUM> (u16, default 64; invalid => crash), --save-text-lockfile, --omit <dev|optional|peer>... (other value => crash 'invalid `omit` value'), --lockfile-only, --linker isolated|hoisted (invalid => exit 1), --minimum-release-age <NUM seconds>, --minimum-release-age-excludes <STR>..., --cpu/--os/--libc <STR>... (values *, any, none, !name negation; unknown name fatal with valid list: cpu arm,arm64,ia32,mips,mipsel,ppc,ppc64,s390,s390x,x32,x64; os aix,darwin,freebsd,linux,openbsd,sunos,win32,android; libc glibc,musl), --use-system-ca, --use-openssl-ca, --use-bundled-ca, -h/--help, plus a list of ignored runtime no-value flags (--bun, --watch, --hot, --smol, ...). Log level precedence: --silent > --verbose (or global verbose) > --quiet > default. Unknown long flag => 'bun <cmd> has no --<flag> flag.' + note, exit 1. Foreign npm/yarn/pnpm flag aliasing/ignoring (FOREIGN_FLAGS/IGNORED_FOREIGN_FLAGS) only applies to install/add/remove/update, NOT to pm/pack/publish/audit/why/etc. Conflicts: --production+--trust and --frozen-lockfile+--trust crash. -g forced off for link/unlink; -g with prune is an error ('--global cannot be used with bun prune' + note that global folder is the link registry). --cwd chdir is applied once (first parse); relative to cwd if starting with '.'. Positional 'ci' implies frozen lockfile. --filter accepted only for outdated/install/update/add/remove/prune/pm/publish; --json only for audit/pm/info. Paths for --config/--cache-dir/--cafile resolved relative to start dir once.

features.name: bun pm per-subcommand flag gating
features.details: PM_PARAMS adds: -a/--all, --trusted, --hash, --json, --diff <STR>..., --raw, --unformatted, --unminify, --minify, -w/--ignore-space, --name-only, --stat, -U/--unified <STR>, -F/--filter <STR>..., -D/--dev, --long, --destination <STR>, --filename <STR>, --gzip-level <STR>, --git-tag-version <BOOL>, --no-git-tag-version, --allow-same-version, -m/--message <STR>, --preid <STR>, --top, --depth <NUM>, --max-age <NUM>. PM_SUBCOMMAND_FLAGS restricts: cache:[--max-age]; diff:[--diff,--json,--raw,--unformatted,--unminify,--minify,--ignore-space,--name-only,--stat,--unified]; licenses:[--json,--filter,--dev,--long]; ls (and alias list):[--all,--trusted,--depth]; pack:[--destination,--filename,--gzip-level]; pkg:[--json]; trust:[--all]; version:[--git-tag-version,--no-git-tag-version,--allow-same-version,--message,--preid]; view:[--json]; why:[--top,--depth]. Using a gated flag with another subcommand => '<flag> is only supported by `bun pm X`, ...' exit 1. --git-tag-version=false equals --no-git-tag-version. --unified must parse as usize (error 'invalid --unified value'); --max-age must be u32 days ('invalid --max-age value'); --depth usize ('invalid depth value'). no_project_ok (missing package.json OK) for: '' (help), diff, view, cache, whoami, default-trusted; bin/ls/list only with -g; also bun info.

features.name: bun pm dispatcher, aliases, help
features.details: Top-level aliases: 'bun whoami' and 'bun list' route to PackageManagerCommand; 'list' maps to 'ls'. 'bun pm' with leading 'pm' positional dropped. Missing package.json (when not no_project_ok) => 'No package.json was found for directory "<cwd>"' + note 'Run "bun init"...' exit 1. -g triggers setup_global_dir. Unknown subcommand => prints pm help then '"X" unknown command' exit 1; no subcommand => help exit 0. Help lists: scan, pack (+flags), bin (-g), ls (names..., --all, --trusted, --prod, -g), why, diff, licenses, whoami, view, version, pkg get/set/delete/fix, hash, hash-string, hash-print, cache, cache rm (--dry-run), cache prune (--max-age, --dry-run), cache pack|unpack <file>, fetch, migrate, untrusted, trust (--all, --dry-run), default-trusted. Lockfile load errors: NotFound => 'missing lockfile[, nothing to X]' + note 'run bun install first' exit1; Err => 'failed to <verb> lockfile: <err>' exit 1 (suppressed with --silent).

features.name: bun pm bin [-g]
features.details: Prints absolute path of options.bin_path joined to top-level dir (local: <project>/node_modules/.bin; -g: global bin dir, default ~/.bun/bin). Extra blank line when stdout is a terminal. With -g and colored stderr, warns '\nwarn: not in $PATH' if the bin dir (trailing slash stripped; case-insensitive on Windows) isn't a PATH entry. Works without package.json when -g.

features.name: bun pm ls / bun list
features.details: Lists installed deps from lockfile filtered to what's on disk. Header '<cwd> node_modules (<N> installed)' then flat '├── name@resolution' / '└── ...' of root direct deps (sorted by name, deduped when same resolution unless workspace-member rows; filtered by behavior enabled for features). --all: full nested tree of node_modules folders (├──/└──/│ glyphs, header '<cwd> node_modules'). --trusted: only trusted deps (trustedDependencies from package.json files, else default list) printed as a flat list. Names as positionals: search all installed packages by dependency name, flat list, exit 1 'no packages match: a, b' if none. --production/--omit exclude groups and packages only reachable through them (reachable::packages). --depth only accepts 0 (error 'bun pm ls --depth only accepts 0 ...'); --depth takes precedence over --all. Installed check: resolution root/symlink always; workspace -> member dir exists; else node_modules/<dir>/<alias> exists or (isolated) found in node_modules/.bun store (name@version key or with '+' peer suffix). No node_modules => lists every lockfile-resolved dep. -g with no global lockfile prints '<global dir> node_modules (0 installed)'. Control chars escaped in output.
features.bun_source: submodule/bun/src/runtime/cli/package_manager_command.rs L41-109, L596-770, L858-1052; BunStore lookup submodule/bun/src/runtime/cli/pm_licenses_command.rs L536-596

features.name: bun pm hash / hash-string / hash-print
features.details: Loads lockfile from cwd (handles errors with nothing_to='hash'). hash: recompute meta hash (has_meta_hash_changed) then print fmt_meta_hash with no trailing newline. hash-string: prints the string used to compute the hash (has_meta_hash_changed(print_string=true)) and does not print hash. hash-print: prints hash stored in lockfile without recomputing. Legacy 'bun ./bun.lockb --hash' path: print_hash reads a lockfile file and prints its meta hash.

features.name: bun pm cache (print path)
features.details: No action: prints real path of the install cache directory (no trailing newline) using get_cache_directory (honors bunfig/npmrc/env). Cache dir resolution (fetch_cache_directory_path): $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR > configured (--cache-dir / bunfig install.cache.dir) > $BUN_INSTALL/install/cache > ($XDG_CACHE_HOME or $HOME)/.bun/install/cache > cwd fallback node_modules/.bun-cache; ~ expanded. Extra positional after 'cache' (other than rm/prune/pack/unpack) => 'unexpected argument "X"' + usage 'bun pm cache [rm | prune | pack <file> | unpack <file>]' exit 1.

features.name: bun pm cache rm [--dry-run]
features.details: Deletes contents (not the dir itself; may be symlink/mount) of cache dir. Dir chosen ONLY from process env ($BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR), --cache-dir, ~/.bunfig.toml install cache dir, or $BUN_INSTALL — project bunfig/.npmrc/.env ignored (security). Extra arg ('rm <pkg>') is an error. Refuses ('refusing to clear "<path>": is or contains <X>' + note listing sources) if the real path is or contains: $HOME, the bun executable, $BUN_INSTALL, project dir, cwd (compared via real paths). Missing dir is fine. Counts bunx cached packages before deletion. Output 'Cleared 'bun install' cache' or dry-run 'dry run: would delete 'bun install' cache at <path>'. If <cache>/links (global store) exists: note 'global store was|would be removed too, run bun install in each project that uses it'. Also deletes bunx temp dirs in platform temp dir: '.bunx-<uid>' root and legacy 'bunx-<uid>-<pkg>' entries; prints '(Would clear|Cleared) N cached 'bunx' packages'. Exit 1 if any deletion error.

features.name: bun pm cache prune [--max-age <days>] [--dry-run]
features.details: Same cache-dir selection and protection as rm. Default max age 30 days (DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_DAYS). Walks cache root and @scope dirs; for each package entry (classified by CacheEntryKind::from_name: name@version..., @G@, @GH@, @T@), last_used = max(mtime, atime); removed if last_used <= now - max_age*86400. Dry run prints '- <name>' per entry (no sizes to avoid refreshing atime). Non-dry-run deletes tree, sums file sizes (lstat, no symlink follow), removes empty scope dirs, and in index dirs removes dangling symlinks then empty index dirs. Global store (<cache>/links), git clones, manifests kept. Missing cache dir: 'Done! No cache directory (nothing to prune)'. Messages: 'Done! Checked N packages, none older than D days (nothing to prune)'; dry: 'N packages older than D days can be removed (checked C)' + 'Run without --dry-run to remove them.'; real: 'Removed N packages older than D days (<size>)[, X failed]'. Exit 1 on failures. DT_UNKNOWN entries lstat'd.

features.name: bun pm cache pack <file> / unpack <file>
features.details: Exactly one <file> (relative to original cwd) else usage error exit 1. pack requires lockfile. Binary format: 16-byte MAGIC 'BUNCACHEPACK\0v1\n' then little-endian records: u8 kind | u32 path_len | path | u32 mode | u64 size | bytes. Kinds: 0 END, 1 PACKAGE (path = cache folder name, ascending order; bytes = nested records), 2 FILE, 3 SYMLINK, 4 DIRECTORY (precedes its contents), 5 CHECKSUM (u64 wyhash of folder name then package bytes). Max path 4095 (or MAX_PATH-1). Entries: every lockfile package (npm/git/github/local+remote tarball; not bundled; tarballs need supported integrity) by unpatched cache subpath; 'expected' = matches current cpu/os/libc; missing expected => warn 'skipping N packages not in cache (run bun install first)'. Output written via temp file renamed over destination; uncompressed. unpack: validates entire pack before writing (refuses damaged/incomplete as a whole), validates names (safe relative paths, ASCII graphic, components <=255, Windows-safe, entry_tag shapes name@x.y.z[-hex16][+HEX16][@@host[__hex16]]@@@n, @T@, @GH@, @G@), stages in private temp dir, rename-no-replace into cache (never overwrites existing), creates index links. Output 'Packed N packages (F files, size) into <file> [time]' / 'Unpacked N packages (X new, Y already cached, size) [time]'; dry-run 'Would pack'/'Would unpack' with no writes; warn 'ignoring N incomplete cache entries, bun install will re-download'. Errors 'bun pm cache <verb> failed: <err>' exit 1.

features.name: bun pm fetch
features.details: Resolves like install and downloads every dependency into cache without node_modules, scripts, or package.json/lockfile writes (populate_package_cache::fetch). With lockfile downloads only missing tarballs/git commits; all workspaces in lockfile even if not on disk. Skips other os/cpu unless --os/--cpu given. -g fetches global packages' deps. --dry-run counts missing, downloads none. Security scanner not run (verbose note 'packages are not scanned until bun install runs the security scanner'). Header 'bun pm fetch v<ver>' unless --silent/--no-summary. Summary: '(Would fetch|Fetched) N packages into cache [time]' / 'Done! N packages already in cache' / 'Done! No packages to fetch' then 'Cache: <abs path>'. Exit 1 on log errors or failed installs.

features.name: bun pm migrate [--dry-run] [--force]
features.details: Without --force, errors '<bun.lock|bun.lockb> already exists\nrun with --force to overwrite' exit 1. Detects other lockfiles in order npm-shrinkwrap.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock (v1 + berry), pnpm-lock.yaml; tries each, on failure warns 'cannot migrate X (err), trying Y'. None => 'could not find any other lockfile' exit 1. --dry-run prints 'dry run: would write <bun.lock|bun.lockb>' and writes nothing. Otherwise writes migrated package.json edits (write_migrated) then saves lockfile in configured format.

features.name: bun pm untrusted
features.details: Header 'bun pm untrusted v<ver>' on stderr. Loads lockfile (update_lockfile_if_needed), reads trustedDependencies from current package.json files. Finds installed deps whose lifecycle scripts would be blocked: isolated linker with node_modules/.bun present => iterate store folders; otherwise iterate install tree (excludes bundled). Root/workspace scripts always run so not listed; trusted (trustedDependencies or default list) not listed; ENOENT ignored. Prints each with scripts (PrintFormat::Untrusted), ' alias of "<name>"' when alias differs, and 'cannot trust by name: add it to your package.json dependencies' for non-registry deps (tarball/git/file/link) not declared in project/workspace package.json. Zero => 'Found 0 untrusted dependencies with scripts...' + docs link. Footer suggests 'bun pm [-g ]trust'.

features.name: bun pm trust <names...> [--all] [--dry-run]
features.details: Requires names or --all ('expected package names(s) or --all'). Errors: --ignore-scripts => 'lifecycle scripts are disabled (ignore-scripts), nothing to run'; frozen lockfile (non-dry-run) => 'lockfile is frozen. refusing to update package.json & lockfile'. Matches blocked packages by trusted name (case-sensitive eql_long); an alias arg notes 'X is an alias of Y, run bun pm trust Y'. Undeclared non-registry packages skipped with note. Packages in isolated global store (store entry is a symlink) are Deferred: trusted but scripts run on next install ('N trusted packages linked from the global store: run bun install ...'). Zero to trust => '0 scripts ran...' error listing names, crash. --dry-run prints scripts and 'dry run: would run N scripts across M packages' + 'would add to trustedDependencies' list. Opens root package.json RDWR before running any script (error if not writable). Runs scripts deepest-first, grouped by depth, waiting for each depth; concurrency limit max_concurrent_lifecycle_scripts; progress bar. Then edits trustedDependencies in root package.json (preserves trailing newline; pwrite+ftruncate), records ran names in lockfile trusted_dependencies and saves lockfile if any ran. Summary 'N scripts ran across M packages [time]', 'N packages with blocked scripts'.

features.name: bun pm default-trusted
features.details: Prints 'Default trusted dependencies (<N>):' then ' - <name>' for each entry of DEFAULT_TRUSTED_DEPENDENCIES_LIST (src/install/default-trusted-dependencies.txt). No package.json required.

features.name: bun pm version [increment]
features.details: Finds nearest package.json walking up from original cwd. No arg: help showing current version and computed patch/minor/major/prerelease (and prepatch/preminor/premajor when current has '-' or --preid set), from-git, specific, options list. Increments: patch, minor, major, prepatch, preminor, premajor, prerelease, from-git, or a specific semver (loose parse, cleaned; max component 2^53-1). node-semver inc semantics: on prerelease x.y.z-rc, major/minor/patch return the release it was made for; pre* bump then append/increment last numeric id or push '0'; --preid validated (identifiers [0-9A-Za-z-], no leading-zero numerics) and if first id differs => [preid, 0]. Invalid arg => 'Invalid version argument' + valid list exit1. Missing version treated as 0.0.0 for computing. Same version without --allow-same-version => 'Version not changed' exit 1. --dry-run prints 'v<new>' and touches nothing (no scripts). Git: git_tag_version default true; disabled when .git doesn't exist in package dir (file .git for worktrees/submodules counts); unless --force (-f), dirty tree ('git status --porcelain' non-empty) => 'Git working directory not clean.' exit1. Scripts preversion, version, postversion run unless --ignore-scripts; env npm_command=version, npm_package_json, npm_package_name, npm_package_version (old in preversion, new after write), npm_old_version, npm_new_version. Writes package.json preserving indentation & trailing newline. Commit: 'git add package.json', 'git commit -m <msg>' (--message with %s replaced, default 'v<ver>'), 'git tag -a v<ver> -m v<ver>'. from-git: 'git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match=*.*.*', strips non-digit prefix (v1.2.3, name@1.2.3); errors 'No git tags found'/'Tag is not a valid version'. Requires git in PATH ('git must be installed to use bun pm version ...'). Prints 'v<new>'.

features.name: bun pm pkg get/set/delete/fix
features.details: Operates on nearest package.json at/above cwd (error 'No package.json found'); root must be object. Key path grammar: dot segments, [index], [] (append, set only), bracketed names literal incl dots (exports[./package.json]). get: no keys => whole file pretty-printed (2-space); one key => value; multiple => object keyed by label; missing => '{}'; name applied to array maps over elements with labels like contributors[0].name; '[]' in get => 'Empty brackets are not valid syntax for retrieving values.'. set key=value ...: errors for missing '=', empty key, empty value; --json parses value as strict JSON (rejects 010, 0x10, 1_000, .5, 5., single quotes) else 'Invalid JSON value for "key"' + note; intermediate missing/null slots created as array if next segment is bracketed numeric/[] else object; only final segment may replace a non-container ('already exists and is not an object or array'); array index > len => out-of-range error with note 'X[] appends'; non-index on array => error; append on non-array => error. delete key ...: removes property or splices array element; no write if nothing removed; [] => error. fix: lowercases name; warns 'No bin file found at <path>' for missing bin object targets. set/delete/fix --dry-run prints resulting JSON instead of writing. Preserves indentation and trailing newline. Unknown subcommand => 'Unknown subcommand' + help exit 1; 'help' or no subcommand prints help.

features.name: bun info / bun pm view
features.details: bun info <pkg>[@version] [property...] [--json]; bun pm view alias. No package.json needed. Empty/'.' spec => root package.json name (if valid npm name), else read package.json name, else basename of top dir; no package.json => 'no package name given and no package.json found'. GET <scope registry>/<encoded name> with Accept: application/json (full manifest) and Authorization if configured; send_with_retries; >=400 => npm response_error. Version selection uses manifest.find_by_spec (range/dist-tag like bun add; default latest). Missing dist-tag: error + up to 10 tags; no matching version: error + 5 most recent versions (prereleases only if no releases). Version entry merged with package-level fields (dist-tags, time; readme only when properties requested); 'versions' replaced by sorted array of valid versions. Properties use pm pkg path grammar, read from version entry then document; missing skipped; none found => 'Property X not found' exit1 (JSON: {error,version,property}). One string property printed raw (JSON-quoted with --json); multiple => 'name = value' lines or JSON object. --json without props prints whole merged manifest. Default text: 'name@version | license | deps: N | versions: N' (license string or {type}, default Proprietary), description, homepage, keywords, bin names, DEPRECATED, dependencies list, dist (tarball, shasum, integrity, unpackedSize), dist-tags (latest cyan, beta blue, other magenta), maintainers (name <email>), Published time (time[version] or modified). All registry strings control-char escaped.

features.name: bun pm licenses [ls|list]
features.details: Optional subcommand list|ls only (else 'unknown subcommand' + note; extra args error). Requires bun.lock and node_modules ('node_modules not found, nothing to list'). Roots: current root/workspace package (from inside workspace only its deps), or --filter workspaces (unmatched patterns warned; none matched => error). Reachability honors --prod/-p/--omit and platform (cpu/os/libc); --dev/-D lists only what devDependencies pull in (error if combined with --prod/--omit=dev). Skips root/workspace/link resolutions. Reads each package's package.json from: isolated store node_modules/.bun/<key>/node_modules/<name>, hoisted tree location, store fallback, then disk index scan; installed copy at a different version listed under installed version; missing counted and warned '<N> packages in bun.lock are not installed and were skipped' + note. License from 'license' (string, {type}, {name}) or 'licenses' (array joined '(A OR B)'), default 'Unknown'; parse failure => Unknown. homepage falls back to repository(.url); author string or 'name <email> (url)'. Sort: Unknown last, case-insensitive ignoring leading '(', then name, semver, version. Text: header 'bun pm licenses v..', groups 'LICENSE (n)' with ├──/└── name@version, ' (dev)' marker for dev-only, --long adds author/description/homepage lines; summary 'N packages across M licenses (checked C packages in bun.lock) [time]'; 'No packages to list'. --json: object keyed by license, arrays of {name, versions[], paths[], license, homepage, author, description}.

features.name: bun pm diff — side resolution and filters
features.details: Args: up to two sides (from positionals and --diff, may be given twice); further args, ':path' args, and 'spec:path' suffixes become file filters (paths/URLs/file:/npm: keep colons). Side classification: starts with '.', '/', '~/' (or Windows drive/backslash) => local; .tgz/.tar.gz/.tar => tarball else folder; else registry name[@version]. Relative local paths resolved against original cwd; ~/ against $HOME. Forms: none => registry latest of package.json name in cwd (cwd package.json first, else root name; error if no valid name) vs cwd folder; one registry 'name' or 'name@b' => lockfile-installed version (search: current workspace's own deps, then root node_modules, then any npm package with that name; alias resolves to real package) vs b (default latest), error if not in lockfile ('give two versions to compare'); 'name@a..b' => a vs b; one folder/tarball => registry latest of its package.json name vs it; two args: bare left name uses installed version; bare right version/range/'latest' reuses left name (or local side's name). Filter matches exact path, directory prefix, bare basename anywhere, or glob (*?[{ or extglob; glob without '/' also tested on basename). No file matches either side => 'no file in either side matches ...' exit 1. Local folder with package.json read 'as published' (pack's published_files: files field, .npmignore/.gitignore, bin) and workspace:/catalog: specs substituted like pack; two folders compared as written. Registry side: manifest + tarball download, integrity checked, registry/scope/auth from bunfig/.npmrc. Outside a project only registry specs and absolute/./ paths. Status line on TTY stderr while fetching. Name validation npm grammar.

features.name: bun pm diff — output modes, normalization and security notes
features.details: Flags: --raw/--unformatted (byte compare, no re-print), --minify (also fold equivalent syntax), --unminify (lockstep-rename short locals in every JS file), -w/--ignore-space ('whitespace only' on terminal), --stat (per-file count + bar), --name-only (A/M/D list), -U/--unified <n> (default 3), --json. Terminal mode: .js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx/.ts/.tsx parsed and canonically re-printed to decide changes (constant folding, quote style, re-wraps, consistent renames via usage profiles); hunks show original lines; folded lines counted ('N folded'), 'formatting only'; '~' marks meaning-moved lines; minified bundles shown via un-minified re-print with line:col; .json/.css shown as canonical print ('normalized'); files > 64 MB (MAX_BYTES) diffed as text ('too large to normalize'); *.map summarized as regenerated. Colors from COLORFGBG or OSC 11 query; truecolor when COLORTERM=truecolor. Control chars/escapes/bidi shown as ␛, ^M, ‹U+202E› (also with NO_COLOR). Piped/NO_COLOR: plain git-applyable unified patch of real contents (empty files, mode changes 'new file mode 100755'/'mode 644 → 755'); binary & source maps under 'diff --bun' header with sizes and SHA-256 prefixes. Binary = NUL near start and not text-like extension/#!/parses as JS. Header 'a@x → b@y', '<n> files changed, A added, R removed (+X -Y lines)'. Notes: registry vs tarball package.json disagreement on dependencies/optionalDependencies/peerDependencies/bin/directories/os/cpu/libc (registry wins), duplicate keys, install scripts added/changed (preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare, prepublish, preuninstall, postuninstall), dep added/removed/changed (range bumps >4 collapsed '… and N more'), main/module/types/bin/exports/engines/license/type/browser/imports/directories/os/cpu/libc/bundle(d)Dependencies changed/added/removed, new imports of builtins child_process, fs, fs/promises, net, http, https, http2, dgram, dns, tls, vm, worker_threads, os, inspector, new package imports (first 6), growth in eval()/Function()/process.env/fetch()/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket/http(s):// URL (URLs only if >=3), new executable files, now executable, text→binary, terminal escapes, bidi controls, new .node/.sh/.exe files. --json: {from,to,files:[{path,status added|deleted|modified,binary,sourceMap,formattingOnly,linesAdded,linesRemoved,bytesBefore,bytesAfter,modeBefore?,modeAfter?,patch?,sha256Before?,sha256After?}],notes:[],totals:{files,added,deleted,linesAdded,linesRemoved,formattingOnly}}. Exit 0 regardless of differences.

features.name: bun pm pack — flags, scripts, output
features.details: Flags: --dry-run, --destination <dir>, --filename <name> (mutually exclusive: 'cannot use both filename and destination...' crash), --ignore-scripts, --gzip-level <0-9> (default '9'; invalid => 'compression level must be between 0 and 9, received X'), --quiet (only tarball path printed, for $(...)), --silent. Header 'bun pack v<ver>' unless quiet/silent. Requires name and version non-empty strings without '.'/'..' components or '\', ':', NUL ('package.json must have `name` and `version` fields' / 'must be non-empty strings'). Scripts (unless --ignore-scripts, scripts must be object): prepack, prepare before; postpack after (also in dry-run); env npm_command=pack, npm_package_json, npm_package_name, npm_package_version; after scripts package.json re-read (scripts may change version). Tarball name: '<scope>-<name>-<version>.tgz' (leading @ dropped, '/' -> '-'). Destination: --filename relative to original cwd as-is; --destination dir (created) + name; default in package dir. Prints 'packed <size> <path>' per file (package.json first), 'bundled <name>' per bundled dep, tarball path (bare name when default), 'Total files', 'Shasum' (sha1 hex), 'Integrity' (sha512-...), 'Unpacked size', 'Packed size', 'Bundled deps'. Dry run: no tarball, sizes from stat, no shasum/integrity. --verbose prints 'ignore [kind:pattern] path' for excluded entries. Progress bar in files.

features.name: pack file selection (files, ignore files, defaults, bins)
features.details: Root lockfiles never packed: package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb, bun.lock. Never-packable (strict): .git, .npmrc, .bun-pack.*.tmp. Overridable default ignores: .*.swp, ._*, .DS_Store, .gitignore, .hg, .npmignore, .lock-wscript, .svn, .wafpickle-*, CVS, npm-debug.log, .env.production, bunfig.toml. Always included at root: package.json, LICENSE/LICENCE/README (+any .ext; case-insensitive except Linux/Android), CHANGELOG (only via ignore path). Root node_modules skipped (bundled deps handled separately). With 'files' array (must be array of strings else error): entries normalized posix; '!' entries are exclusions; include patterns matched against subpath (index.js root only, **/index.js any depth), trailing '/' dirs-only, negations narrow included dirs; matched dirs packed whole minus negated patterns and nested node_modules. Without files: walk tree depth-first; per dir read .npmignore else .gitignore (BOM stripped, # comments, CRLF, git trailing-space rules with '\ ' escape); patterns: leading/middle slash => rel path, trailing slash dirs-only, '!' negation (multiple ! = one, '!(' escaped); later patterns win; excluded dir with negation reaching below is walk-only (entries stay excluded unlike npm). Only regular files/dirs (symlinks skipped; DT_UNKNOWN lstat'd; subdirs opened no-follow). Bins: 'bin' string/object (empty counts absent) or directories.bin added first and get +x (perm |= 0o111); bin path must be inside package, not package.json, not under .git/.npmrc. Dedupe of queued paths; sorted order. Ignore file read errors are fatal.

features.name: pack bundledDependencies
features.details: Reads bundledDependencies then bundleDependencies: array of strings or boolean true (=all keys of dependencies); other => 'expected `X` to be a boolean or an array of strings' crash. Each listed dep resolved via node_modules ancestry (not above project/workspace root, real paths); missing deps skipped if not in dependencies or if optional (npm-like), otherwise 'bundled dependency "X" is not installed' crash. Transitive dependencies/optionalDependencies of bundled packages placed at node_modules/<name> or nested node_modules/a/node_modules/b to preserve resolution; cycles through two versions => 'bundled dependencies form a cycle' crash. Installed copies packed whole minus default ignores and nested node_modules; workspace/linked folders (no node_modules in real path) packed as packages via published_files, their package.json workspace:/catalog: specs rewritten; folder without package.json packed as directory honoring ignore files. Counted in 'Bundled deps'.

features.name: pack workspace:/catalog: substitution
features.details: In dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, optionalDependencies: 'workspace:^'/'~'/'*' => '^ver'/'~ver'/'ver' of the named workspace; 'workspace:<name>@<range>' alias (range ''/'*'/'^'/'~' use version, else range kept) => same name gives version else 'npm:<ws>@<ver>'; 'workspace:<dir>' => version of workspace at that dir (relative to package dir); 'workspace:<range>' on a dep that is a workspace => range kept. 'catalog:'/'catalog:<name>' => catalog entry (may be workspace: but not another catalog:). Failure => 'Failed to resolve <workspace|catalog> version for "dep" in `group` (reason).' crash. Edited JSON printed preserving indentation and trailing newline; duplicate keys collapsed to last (drop_shadowed_properties).

features.name: Deterministic tarball format and atomic write
features.details: libarchive pax-restricted + gzip; gzip os=Unknown, no timestamp; bytes_in_last_block=1; entries prefixed 'package/'; filetype regular 0o100000; perms from stat (bins +x); mtime fixed 499162500 (1985-10-26T08:15:00Z); package.json written first from edited bytes; file data written in 8192-byte chunks for byte stability; read buffer 512KiB; file shrinking during pack => 'file shrank while packing' crash. Hashes: sha1 shasum, sha512 integrity of compressed bytes. Write: temp '.bun-pack.<rand>.tmp' next to destination (O_EXCL, mode copied from existing writable file else 0666), renamed over destination; exit callback deletes temp on failure; existing symlink at default name replaced but --filename symlink written through; FIFO/device/read-only => in-memory then write in place (O_NOFOLLOW unless --filename); rename failure falls back to in-place write. JS binding read_tarball (entries pathname/kind/perm/contents, size, shasum, integrity) for tests.

features.name: bun publish — flags and flow
features.details: Flags: [tarball path], --access public|restricted (invalid => crash), --tag <STR> (default latest), --otp <STR> (no newline/NUL), --auth-type web|legacy (default web), --gzip-level, --tolerate-republish, -F/--filter, -r/--recursive, --provenance[=bool], --no-provenance, --provenance-file, --dry-run, --ignore-scripts, --registry, plus shared. Header 'bun publish v<ver>'. -r/--filter before 'publish' (e.g. 'bun --filter x publish') => 'refusing to publish: X must come after "publish"' + note. Tarball path with -r/--filter => error. Tarball mode: reads tarball, strips first path component, prints packed list, finds package.json (case-insensitive, top level) and first README*, no scripts run. Directory mode: pack(for_publish) runs prepublishOnly, prepack, prepare, postpack, then after upload publish and postpublish (env npm_command=publish etc.). Errors: missing name/version, invalid semver version ('package.json `version` is not a valid semver version'; leading zeros / v-prefix normalized via published_version), private package ('attempted to publish a private package'; JS truthiness of private), restricted unscoped ('unable to restrict access to unscoped package'). Tag rules: tag that is a version/range => 'invalid tag'; prerelease with no tag => 'prerelease needs a tag' + note. Provenance requested by --provenance/--provenance-file, publishConfig.provenance, NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE/npm_config_provenance, or .npmrc provenance => '... is not supported yet' crash (precedence CLI > publishConfig > env > .npmrc; false allowed). Requires credentials ('missing authentication (run `bunx npm login`)'). Prints 'Tag: X\nAccess: <access|default>\nRegistry: <href>/' then ' + name@version[ (dry-run)]'. --tolerate-republish: GET package doc, if version exists warn 'Registry already knows about version X; skipping.' and exit 0. NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN honored.

features.name: publishConfig handling
features.details: From package.json (post-script): publishConfig.tag and .access used only if CLI not given; invalid access => crash. publishConfig.registry replaces default registry only (unless --registry on CLI); '@scope:registry' key replaces scope registry. Credentials: from registry with same URL in bunfig/.npmrc, //host/:_authToken lines (https only for publishConfig URLs), else inherited from previous registry only if same origin and path under it; otherwise missing auth error. Env vars not expanded in publishConfig URLs. Recursive publish restores PublishTarget between packages.

features.name: Publish request body, headers, OTP/web auth
features.details: PUT <registry>/<encoded name>. Body JSON: {_id,name,'dist-tags':{tag:version},versions:{version:normalized},access:'public'|'restricted'|null,_attachments:{'<name>-<version>.tgz':{content_type:'application/octet-stream',data:base64,length}}}; build tag stripped from version. Normalized package.json (minified): version, _id 'name@ver', _integrity, _nodeVersion (REPORTED_NODEJS_VERSION), _npmVersion '10.8.3', integrity, shasum, readme/readmeFilename (first README file from readdir, not symlink, only if no readme field), dist {integrity, shasum, tarball 'http://<registry host+path>/<name>/-/<name>-<version>.tgz' always http}, bin normalized to object (string bin keyed by package name; keys './' stripped; root/outside paths dropped; warn 'bin X does not exist'; directories.bin expanded recursively to {basename: path}). Headers: accept */*, accept-encoding gzip,deflate, authorization, content-type application/json, npm-auth-type (legacy when OTP given, else --auth-type or web), npm-otp, npm-command publish, user-agent '<UA> <os> <arch> workspaces/<bool>[ ci/<name>]', Connection keep-alive, Host, Content-Length. Response <400 ok. 401: www-authenticate 'ipaddress' => 'login is not allowed from your IP address'; 'otp' or body contains 'one-time pass' => OTP flow; otherwise 'unable to authenticate, need: X'. OTP: if JSON body has authUrl+doneUrl (doneUrl same protocol/host/port as registry) show boxed URL ('press ENTER to open in browser' when http(s) & printable; ENTER thread opens browser), poll doneUrl: 202 sleep retry-after secs (default 500ms), 200 token (validated) used as OTP; else prompt 'This operation requires a one-time password.\nEnter OTP: '. Retries PUT with npm-otp. npm-notice header printed as note.

features.name: bun publish --recursive / --filter
features.details: -r: root package + every workspace; --filter: matching workspaces. Order: dependencies before dependents (workspace_manifests::selected_in_dependency_order). Skips private ('skipped X: private') and versions already on registry ('skipped name@ver: already on the registry', checked with credentials before scripts). Packs every package first (printing magenta name), then publishes each in order; first failure ends run; rerun skips published.

features.name: bun audit
features.details: Positionals: only 'fix' allowed ('unknown subcommand "X" for bun audit' + note). Flags: --json, --audit-level low|moderate|high|critical (invalid => crash; unknown severity treated as moderate), --ignore <GHSA or numeric id>... (matches id exactly or substring of advisory url), -p/--prod/--production, --omit dev|optional|peer, --latest (only with fix else crash), --dry-run (fix). Reads bun.lock (no node_modules needed). Collects npm-resolved packages (excluding root; reachable filter when omitting), grouped by registry (scope registry per package); body {name:[versions]} gzip-compressed (level 6) POST <registry>/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk with accept/content-type application/json, content-encoding gzip, authorization; retried. Non-default registry failures => warn '<registry> did not answer the audit request (reason); skipped pkgs' and counted skipped; default registry failure or non-http protocol => fatal 'POST <url> - <reason>' exit 1. Response validation: empty, non-JSON, or not {name:[objects]} => 'invalid audit response from <registry>: <reason>' exit 1. Advisory fields severity (default moderate), title (default 'Vulnerability found'), url, vulnerable_versions, id (string or number). Report: per package name with installed versions, severity, title, ranges, url, dependency paths (direct dependency, workspace:<name> prefix, BFS through dependents), summary 'N vulnerabilities (x critical, y high, z moderate, w low)' + hints 'bun audit fix' / 'bun audit fix --latest'; clean: 'No vulnerabilities found' with (N below --audit-level=X, N ignored, N skipped). --json prints raw merged registry JSON (unfiltered), exit code still filtered. Exit 0 if no remaining vulns after level/ignore else 1. Header 'bun audit[ fix] v<ver>'.

features.name: bun audit fix [--latest] [--dry-run] [--json]
features.details: No extra args. Requires lockfile matching package.json ('bun.lock does not match package.json, nothing to fix'); refuses frozen/--production/--no-save (needs to write bun.lock). Audits without omit; no advisories => no-vuln message exit 0. Plan: for each npm package instance matched by advisories, fetch fresh manifests (manifest cache disabled); candidates = newer safe releases, then older safe within same major (same minor for 0.x) marked downgrade. Each dependency edge (excluding optional peers) gets lowest candidate satisfying its effective range (overrides/catalogs applied; workspace edges not overridden); common lowest version across upgraders chosen if possible. Exact pins in own package.json/workspace/catalog/overrides treated as ^version (without --latest) and rewritten; --latest lets own ranges be rewritten preserving style (^ stays ^, ~ stays ~, exact/= stays, npm: alias kept; --exact forces exact). Bundled edges never fixed. Peer edges: root copy upgrade wins, peer listed as blocked (peer). Sections: 'fixing:' (name@from → to, package.json[ (overrides|catalog)] edits, (downgrade), (newer than --minimum-release-age)), 'blocked by a dependent's range:' (dependent depends on X@range, hint bun audit fix --latest for own ranges, 'package.json overrides X (selector)'), 'no published version fixes:' with 'bun audit fix --ignore <GHSA>' hint, 'not matched to an installed version:', manifest-unavailable warnings. Installs (security scanner runs), then re-audits saved lockfile; prints 'vulnerable after install:', 'Fixed N vulnerabilities in M packages', 'N vulnerabilities remaining'. --dry-run prints plan only. --json: one object {fixes, blocked, unfixable, unmatched, unaudited, vulnerableAfterInstall, fixed, remaining, dryRun}. Exit by re-audit (or plan with dry-run). patchedDependencies upgraded like others.

features.name: bun why <pattern> / bun pm why
features.details: Flags --top (depth 1, no nested trees), --depth <N> (default 100). Missing pattern => usage, exit 1. Pattern: name[@version]; name supports '*' as exact/prefix*/ *suffix/pre*suf/*contains*; more than one inner '*' invalid. Version: empty/latest/'*' match all; semver query matched against npm version or workspace version; otherwise prefix match on printed resolution. Matches package names and also dependency aliases leading to a package. Peer deps resolved to served copies per linker (isolated served_peers vs hoisted tree served_peers). Unnamed root labeled 'the root package'. No match => 'No packages matching 'X' found in lockfile' exit 1. Output per target 'name@version' then dependents sorted by specifier specificity (exact digits > workspace > ^ > ~ > range ops > .x > other > *), then type (prod>peer>optional peer>optional>dev), then name; prefixes '├─'/'└─'/'│'; type labels dev/peer/optional/optional peer; workspaces shown 'name@workspace' in blue; ' (requires spec)' or ' (requires alias@spec)'. Nested tree of dependents with '*circular', '*deduped' (after subtree >1 line printed; reprinted when previous was cut by depth and now shallower), '(deeper dependencies hidden)', 'No dependents found'. Root omitted from a workspace's dependents.

features.name: bun link (register) / bun link <pkg> / bun unlink
features.details: Link/unlink default to NOT saving (--save to update package.json+lockfile; --no-save default). -g ignored. Missing package.json: created (unless --dry-run). Header 'bun link|unlink v<ver>'. 'bun link' (no args): parses nearest package.json; requires valid npm name ('package.json missing "name"' / 'invalid package.json name'); --dry-run prints 'dry run: would link "name"'; opens global dir (bunfig install.globalDir or default) node_modules, deletes existing entry, creates @scope dir, symlinks (Windows junction) project dir to <global>/node_modules/<name>, links bins into global bin dir; prints 'Success! Registered "name"' with usage hints 'bun link name' and '"name": "link:name"'. 'bun link <pkg>...': runs update_package_json_and_install like add with link: specs ('link:<name>' registered; 'link:<path>' path form handled by install). 'bun unlink': only current dir supported ('bun unlink {packageName} not implemented yet' if args); if not symlinked globally => 'package "X" is not globally linked, so there's nothing to do.' exit 0; dry-run message; unlinks global bins, deletes global entry, prints 'success: unlinked package "X"'. Bare link stays in its folder (no chdir to workspace root).

features.name: bun patch <pkg|path> (prepare)
features.details: Arg: name, name@version, or path containing 'node_modules/' (Windows also node_modules\\); relative path resolved from the workspace dir when run inside a workspace. Missing arg => 'Missing package name to patch' + usage. Looks up package in lockfile (multiple versions => needs version; git/tarball/folder labels supported via dependency@label); refuses folder (file:), link:, workspace packages ('refusing to patch ... edit the folder directly') and bundled deps. --dry-run: 'dry run: would replace <folder> with a copy of <pkg> to edit'. Downloads into cache if missing; if already patched applies existing patch into patched cache entry; replaces node_modules folder with real copy of cache entry (no hard/sym links; isolated store link positions handled), makes bins executable. Prints 'To patch X, edit the following folder: <path>' and 'Once you're done ... bun patch --commit '<path>''; notes if dependents load from global store or install scripts haven't run on this copy. Missing patch file in patchedDependencies => install-time error.

features.name: bun patch --commit / bun patch-commit
features.details: --patches-dir <dir> default 'patches' (absolute inside project written relative; slashes posix). Requires lockfile ('Cannot find lockfile...'). Diffs pristine cache entry vs edited folder using 'git diff --no-index' (git required: 'git must be installed to use bun patch --commit'); non-package files (nested node_modules etc.) temporarily moved aside; stderr truncated to 256 bytes on failure. Empty diff: if package already patched => removes patch (entry from patchedDependencies + lockfile, deletes patch file unless shared, reinstall original); else 'No changes detected' (and lists other isolated store folders to commit). Binary changes => error listing 'Binary files ... differ' lines. Patch filename '<name>@<version>.patch' with URL credentials stripped and chars / \\ space \n \r \t : ? * " < > | percent-escaped. Patch verified by applying to scratch copy (parse errors/skipped sections fail); failure => no changes. --dry-run: 'dry run: would write <path> and add <key> to patchedDependencies'. Otherwise sets patchedDependencies[name@version] = path, runs install; patch file written only after install checks pass (security scanner refusal etc. leaves everything untouched). Patched cache entries suffixed '_patch_hash=<hex of first 8 bytes of sha1 of patch>'. patchedDependencies read only from root package.json. Install: missing patch file => 'patch file not found' + recreate hint; skipped sections warned 'skipping X: binary file.../no applicable changes'.

features.name: bun prune
features.details: No positional args. Flags: -p/--production/--prod, --omit dev|optional|peer, --check (dry-run + exit 1 if removable), --dry-run, --os/--cpu/--libc, --linker isolated|hoisted (tie-break), -F/--filter, --silent, --cwd. -g rejected. Missing package.json => 'missing package.json, nothing to prune'. Missing lockfile => error + note. Forces frozen lockfile; lockfile must match package.json ('bun.lock does not match package.json, nothing to prune'). No node_modules => 'Done! No node_modules folder (nothing to prune)'. Layout detection: dirs for extracted aliases => hoisted vote; symlinks into store => isolated vote; both => configured linker; none => isolated if store has entries else hoisted. Always from workspace root covering all workspaces' node_modules; --filter limits to selected workspaces plus shared locations (root node_modules / .bun) keeping what unselected workspaces need. Removes packages not in lockfile install tree, dev-only (with --production), platform-disabled, stale .bun store entries, leftover .bun-tmp-* staging and .old_modules-* (unless an install is running via staging lock), dangling .bin links, unhoisted links. Never removes workspace folders, used .bin entries, dot-dirs, plain files, anything outside node_modules. Matches by name; wrong-version packages left; nested copy removed only once correct version above it (else warning). Symlinked node_modules (root/workspace/.bun) => 'cannot prune symlink X' + note, exit 1. Output: '- name@version (folder)' rows, 'N packages removed[, X failed] (checked C installed packages) [time]', dry: 'N packages can be removed ...' + '  bun prune <args without --dry-run/--check>'; nothing: 'Done! Checked N installed packages across F folders (nothing to prune)'. Deletion failures => continue, exit 1. Never contacts registry/runs scripts/modifies lockfile.

features.name: bun dedupe
features.details: No positional args. Flags: --check (dry-run, exit 1 if duplicates), --dry-run (exit 0), --lockfile-only, --frozen-lockfile/--production/--no-save (fail with 'N duplicate versions can be removed, but <--no-save was passed|--frozen-lockfile was passed|--production implies --frozen-lockfile>' + note), --linker, --silent, --cwd. Missing package.json/lockfile errors; lockfile must match package.json ('bun.lock does not match package.json, nothing to dedupe'); auto-migrates npm/yarn/pnpm lockfiles. Algorithm: groups npm-resolved versions per name (package_index), sorted newest first; repeatedly re-points each edge to an already-locked version satisfying its effective range (overrides/catalogs), keeping the fewest (preferring newer), may move direct deps older; dist-tag/git/tarball deps keep resolution; patchedDependencies versions pinned and any removed version needed to reach a patched package kept ('kept X (needed to reach patched Y)'); isolated peer variants not duplicates. Rows '↳ name from → to' ('~'/'->' without color), '(removed)', '(downgrade)' when all survivors lower major. Summary 'N duplicate versions removed, M packages installed (checked C packages in bun.lock) [time]'; none: '🎉 No duplicates — checked N packages in bun.lock, every one already resolves to a single version'; check/dry: 'N duplicate versions can be removed (checked ...)' + 'bun dedupe'. Forces lockfile save then installs. install/update also collapse newly appended versions (collapse_appended), never touching existing ones.

areas.notes:
I read the source for every command in this area and cross-checked it against docs/pm/cli/*.mdx. A few behaviors matter for the port:
- Flag parsing for every PM command comes from one module: src/install/PackageManager/CommandLineArguments.rs. It holds the per-command param tables, the per-pm-subcommand flag restrictions, and the cross-flag conflict checks. Port it first.
- `bun pm cache rm` and `bun pm cache prune` never take the cache dir from project config (bunfig, .npmrc or .env). They also refuse dirs that contain HOME, the bun executable, $BUN_INSTALL, the project or the cwd. This is a safety rule, so it has to carry over exactly.
- Pack output is byte-deterministic: fixed mtime 499162500, pax-restricted tar, gzip with no timestamp and os=Unknown, 8 KiB write chunks, last-block padding 1. Each matters if fnpm tarballs must match bun or npm shasums.
- `bun pm diff` is very large (~5k lines across pm_diff_*.rs) and includes JS/CSS/JSON canonical re-printing that depends on bun's parser and printer. My entry lists its user-visible behavior; I did not read pm_diff_semantic.rs, pm_diff_relayout.rs or pm_diff_profile.rs past their header comments.
- `bun pm migrate` reuses the install-side migrators (src/install/migration.rs, yarn.rs, yarn_berry.rs, pnpm.rs), which belong to the lockfile area. The same goes for `bun link <pkg>`'s `link:<path>` resolution and the security scanner internals.
- src/install/cache_publish.rs is internal staging for cache entries and has no user-visible surface, so it has no entry.
- `bun pm hash-print` has no dedicated test (no grep hits).
- I could not find a dedicated `bun pm cache prune` test file. bun-pm.test.ts contains 'prune' and 'max-age' strings, which is where it is likely covered.
- `bun outdated` and `bun update` belong to another area and are not covered.

features.name: `bun run <script>` vs bare `bun <script>` (AutoCommand)
features.details: Both route through exec_auto_or_run -> RunCommand::exec_with_cfg. ExecCfg differs: RunCommand={bin_dirs_only:false, log_errors:true, allow_fast_run_for_extensions:false}; AutoCommand={bin_dirs_only:true (only searches the prepended node_modules/.bin dirs, i.e. PATH minus original PATH; NOT the system PATH), log_errors: !if_present, allow_fast_run_for_extensions:true}. `bun run` with nothing found exits 1; bare `bun x` falls through silently if log_errors false. Leading positional 'run' is stripped. Dispatch priority: --parallel/--sequential -> multi_run; else --filter/--workspaces -> filter_run; else single run. For fnpm (no runtime), `fnpm run` should behave like RunCommand; an auto mode `fnpm <script>` is optional.

features.name: Flag/positional boundary and passthrough
features.details: clap stop_after_positional_at: RunCommand=2 (`run` + script name), AutoCommand=1. features.name: pre<name> / post<name> lifecycle hooks
features.details: If scripts["pre"+name] exists it runs first (no passthrough args), then main (with passthrough), then scripts["post"+name] (no passthrough). Any non-zero exit of pre or main exits the bun process immediately with that code, so later scripts never run. Each invocation sets npm_lifecycle_event to its own name (prebuild/build/postbuild) and npm_lifecycle_script to its raw (unrewritten) content. All three share the same env/PATH; shell resolved from ORIGINAL PATH (before .bin prepend). No `--ignore-scripts` style suppression for run pre/post. npm's builtin hook names (prepare, prepublishOnly...) are NOT special in run.
