features.name: Shell selection (--shell / run.shell)
features.details: ctx.debug.use_system_shell default = !cfg!(windows) => POSIX default 'system', Windows default 'bun' (Bun's cross-platform shell interpreter). `--shell bun|system` (run/auto only); other values -> error 'Expected --shell to be one of 'bun' or 'system'. Received: "x"', exit 1. bunfig `[run] shell = "bun"|"system"` (error 'Invalid shell, only 'bun' and 'system' are supported' / 'Expected string'). System shell discovery (find_shell, cached once/process): search PATH for bash, sh, zsh in that order; then hardcoded /bin/bash, /usr/bin/bash, /usr/local/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/sh, /usr/bin/zsh, /usr/local/bin/zsh, /system/bin/sh (Android), must be executable; none -> MissingShell error. Windows system shell = C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe with '/c'. POSIX invoked as `<shell> -c <script>` (argv0 = shell path). For script runs the shell is searched on the ORIGINAL PATH (shell_path param), not the .bin-augmented PATH. NOTE: with --filter/--parallel the POSIX path ALWAYS uses system `sh -c` (ScriptArgv), and Windows uses `bun exec --no-env-file <script>` regardless of --shell. fnpm without a bundled shell interpreter: needs system shell everywhere (cmd.exe on Windows, or ship a portable shell).

features.name: Rewrite npm/yarn/pnpm/npx invocations inside scripts to bun
features.details: replace_package_manager_run scans script bytes; a match only at a token start (previous char is space, '"', or '\'' or start of string). Rules: 'yarn run ' -> 'bun run'; 'yarn npm ...' kept; 'yarn -flag' kept; 'yarn <cmd>' where cmd NOT in YARN_COMMANDS (access add audit autoclean bin cache check config create dedupe dlx exec explain generate-lock-entry generateLockEntry global help import info init install licenses link list login logout node npm outdated owner pack patch plugin policies publish rebuild remove run set tag team unlink unplug up upgrade upgrade-interactive upgradeInteractive version versions why workspace workspaces) -> 'bun run <cmd>' (only if followed by another space); 'npm run ' -> 'bun run' + workspace-flag translation; 'npx ' -> 'bun x '; 'pnpm run ' -> 'bun run '; 'pnpm dlx ' -> 'bun x '; 'pnpx ' -> 'bun x '. npm run workspace translation (append_npm_run_in_workspaces): considers args up to first ; & | CR LF; bails (no translation) if command contains ' " ( ) $ ` \ #. Tokens: '-w X'/'--workspace X'/'--workspace=X'/'-w=X' -> ' --filter=X' (prefix './' if X contains '/' and doesn't start with @ . /); '--workspaces'/'--ws' -> ' --workspaces'; '--if-present' -> ' --if-present'; '--' passes rest; other tokens kept as rest. Only applied if a workspace selector was found; flags are moved before the script name. Workspace value starting with '-' or containing < > aborts. Binary name is 'bun' (release) / 'bun-debug'. Applied in bun run, --filter, --parallel/--sequential, and install lifecycle scripts. For fnpm: rewrite to 'fnpm run'/'fnpm x'.

In --filter / multi-run each package gets its own PATH built from that package's dir (computed per package, swapped into env per spawn, restored after). bunx prepends '<cache>/node_modules/.bin' when running from its cache.

[bun-runtime-specific: aliasing node to the runtime; EXCLUDE for fnpm, but fnpm must still set npm_node_execpath/NODE to the real node if found]. bunfig run.bun=false disables.

features.name: Workspace discovery for --filter / --workspaces
features.details: Walk up from cwd looking for package.json with 'workspaces' (array, or object with 'packages' array; non-string item -> 'Failed to parse "workspaces" property: all items must be strings' exit 1; wrong shape stops walk). Each pattern P becomes glob 'P/package.json' rooted at that dir; '!' entries are negations (NegatedWorkspaces: stored posix, './' stripped, trailing '/' stripped; 'dir/**' also excludes 'dir'; negation applies only to glob matches, never to literally listed paths). If no workspace root found: glob '**/package.json' from cwd. Glob walker skips dirs named '.', 'node_modules', '.git'; does not loop on self-referential symlinks. --workspaces excludes the root package itself and uses pattern '*'. Each package.json parsed with deps+devDeps+optionalDeps (IncludeDependencies::Main) and scripts; unparsable -> warning 'Failed to read "path", skipping this workspace package'; too-long paths reported, others still run.

features.name: --filter / -F pattern grammar
features.details: Repeatable. Grammar: '!'* (each toggles negation) then optional '...' prefix (dependents) with optional '^' (exclude self), optional '...' suffix (dependencies) with optional '^' before it (exclude self), around base. Base: '*' or '**' = All (unnamed packages excluded unless root); '{dir}' = Subtree (every workspace whose dir or ancestor matches the glob, resolved from cwd); starts with '.' = Path glob on absolute posix dir (resolved against cwd, trailing slash stripped; './packages' matches nothing, './packages/*' matches children); otherwise Name glob on package.json name (full-name match; '*' does not cross '/'; 'core' doesn't match '@acme/core'). Relation with empty base -> error '--filter "x" is missing a workspace name or path'. Path too long -> error. Selection = union of positive patterns minus union of negated; if no positive patterns, start from All. Relations walk a graph built from workspace dependency NAMES (deps/dev/optional) via BFS; transitive. Pattern matching nothing: warning 'No workspace packages matched the filter "x"'; nothing selected at all -> error 'No workspace packages matched the filter(s) "a", "b"' (Global::crash, exit 1) unless --if-present (exit 0); --workspaces with none -> 'No workspace packages found' exit 1. Only a ./path pattern selects a package.json without a name. Same selector logic shared with install/add/remove/update/outdated/prune/pm licenses (RootSelection Implicit vs ExplicitOnly).

features.name: --filter script run: parallel with topological order
features.details: Script name = positionals[1] (after 'run') or positionals[0]. For each selected package (discovery order) with scripts: add handles for pre<name>, <name>, post<name> that exist. Each command = rewritten script + passthrough args (NOTE: passthrough appended to pre AND post too in filter mode) + NUL; run via ScriptArgv (POSIX `<sh> -c`, Windows `bun exec --no-env-file`). cwd = package dir, PATH = per-package .bin chain. stdin ignored, stdout/stderr piped. Concurrency: UNLIMITED — every handle with no pending deps starts immediately. Dependency edges: package A waits for all handles of workspace package B if A's deps/devDeps/optionalDeps names B (by name; duplicates names allowed). Cycle detection (DFS); if any cycle, ALL inter-package ordering is dropped (pre/post order kept). pre->main->post chained within a package (follows_previous compares package.json path). If a script fails or is skipped, the next one in its pre/main/post chain is skipped ('<pkg> <script>: Skipped'), but dependents in other packages still run. No script found anywhere -> 'Script "x" not found in package "a"' / 'in N workspace packages' / 'in N packages matching "pat"' exit 1. With --workspaces a package missing the script -> error unless --if-present. Exit code: first non-zero exit (in handle order), signal -> signal exit code, error -> 1; else 0. Ctrl+C (SIGINT handler, SA_RESETHAND; Windows console ctrl handler): first press sends SIGINT to all children and waits; second press kills immediately. A script is finished only when it exited AND both pipes closed; on exit pipes are drained then force-closed so detached grandchildren holding pipes don't stall.

features.name: --workspaces

features.name: --parallel / --sequential / --no-exit-on-error (Foreman-style)
features.details: --parallel and --sequential together -> 'error: --parallel and --sequential cannot be used together' exit 1. Script names = positionals (minus leading 'run'/'r') PLUS all passthrough args (passthrough is NOT forwarded as args; each becomes another script). None -> '--parallel/--sequential requires at least one script name' exit 1. Single-package mode (no --filter/--workspaces): uses enclosing package.json of cwd; name with '*' is a glob (only '*' wildcard, matches whole name) expanded against script keys, sorted bytewise; no match -> 'No scripts match pattern "x"'; glob w/o scripts -> 'Cannot use glob pattern "x" without package.json scripts'. A name that's not a script runs as a raw shell command; if it looks like a file (starts with '.', '/', '\\' on Windows, or has a runnable JS/TS extension) it's run as '"<bun exe>" <name>' [runtime-specific; fnpm would run 'node <file>' or skip]. Unknown script falls through to shell (non-zero exit). Workspace mode (--filter/--workspaces): packages sorted by display name (name or path relative to root), then dir; for each package and each script name (glob or exact) add configs; label '<pkg>:<script>'. Each name expands to group pre->main->post (pre/post found by exact name). Chaining: within group always sequential; --sequential additionally chains last handle of group N to first of group N+1. NO topological ordering in multi-run (deps ignored), unlimited concurrency in --parallel. Failure (non-zero/signal/error): default aborts — SIGINT to all running and stop starting more; with --no-exit-on-error: skip rest of that group's pre/main/post chain but continue next groups (sequential) / others. Output: each complete line prefixed '<label padded to max label len> | ' colored by group index cycling cyan,yellow,magenta,green,blue,red (colors only if stderr supports ANSI; NO_COLOR respected); child stdout->parent stdout, child stderr->parent stderr; partial final line flushed with newline added; status lines to stderr: 'Done in Nms' (<=1000) / 'Done in N.NNs' / 'Exited with code N' / 'Signaled: SIGNAME' / 'Error'. Exit code: first failure in handle order. Ctrl+C handling same as filter. All scripts in multi-run go through ScriptArgv system shell.

features.name: Install into cache via spawned `bun add` with flock concurrency control
features.details: Create tree dir; acquire exclusive flock on '<tree>.lock' (O_CREAT|O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600; blocking; if lock can't be taken, install without it); re-check tree state under lock (another process may have installed). If Fresh and bin found (and not dist-tag) -> release lock and run. Write '{}\n' package.json if no finished one (marker for unfinished). Spawn `<self> add <install_param> --no-summary` with cwd=tree, inherited stdio, plus: --no-cache (if dist-tag or stale), --force (if no installed copy: relinks, repairs killed install), --verbose, --silent, --trust, --ignore-scripts, CA store flag, --minimum-release-age=, --registry=, --cafile=, --ca= (each). Env: BUN_INTERNAL_BUNX_INSTALL=<tree>, BUN_INTERNAL_BUNX_HAS_COPY=true|false (removed afterward and from repository/git spawns so the tool and nested installs don't inherit them). Install child signal -> re-raise; nonzero -> exit with that code. Then find bin; release lock; run. Failure: with --package and binary_name -> 'Package <pkg> does not provide a binary named <bin>' + hint 'try running without --package...'; else 'could not determine executable to run for package <pkg>'. Exit 1. Concurrent runs of same package don't corrupt the tree; concurrent stale-refresh installs once.

areas.notes:
I read the actual Rust sources: run_command.rs, filter_run.rs, filter_arg.rs, multi_run.rs, bunx_command.rs, exec_command.rs, the Arguments.rs flag tables, mod.rs dispatch, bunfig.rs [run], install/lifecycle_script_runner.rs (script rewriting, ScriptArgv), install/lib.rs (seed_script_env, node shim), workspace_selection.rs (the filter grammar), and the CommandLineArguments.rs bunx flag skipping. Docs: pm/bunx.mdx, pm/filter.mdx, snippets/cli/run.mdx, runtime/bunfig.mdx.

Quirks fnpm should match or fix on purpose:
(1) In --filter and multi-run, each script does not get its own npm_lifecycle_event, npm_lifecycle_script, npm_command or package npm_package_name. The env is the root's. This is likely a bun gap.
(2) In --filter mode, passthrough args are appended to pre and post scripts too. Single-run mode never does this.
(3) In multi-run (--parallel/--sequential), passthrough args become extra script names, not arguments.
(4) --filter has topological order but no concurrency limit. Any dependency cycle drops all cross-package ordering. Multi-run ignores dependency order entirely. The dependency graph uses names in dependencies, devDependencies and optionalDependencies, but not peerDependencies.
(5) Filter and multi-run always use the system `sh -c` on POSIX, whatever --shell says. On Windows they use `bun exec`.
(6) bun run does not set INIT_CWD. Only install lifecycle scripts do (install/PackageManager.rs:1326).
(7) A script exit code of 2 suppresses the 'exited with code' message.
(8) The default shell is 'system' on POSIX and 'bun' on Windows. fnpm will need cmd.exe or a bundled shell on Windows.

Not checked in detail: the Windows BunXFastPath .bunx shim internals (run_command.rs:4060-4248), the full completions code, and IgnoredLongFlags::value_is_next_arg semantics in bun_clap.

Then the project file: `--config/-c <path>` (absolute, or relative to the cwd), else ./bunfig.toml in the cwd. It is auto-loaded for npm-related commands (ALWAYS_LOADS_CONFIG). They are honored when the file is passed with --config.

features.name: install.registry
features.details: Either a string URL or an object {url, username, password, token}. String form: NpmRegistry::from_url parses embedded credentials. `user:pass@host` becomes username+password (percent-decoded). `user@host` alone becomes _auth=base64('user:') (empty password, like npm). `:token@host` becomes a Bearer token. The URL is stored without credentials. Object form: if any of username/password/token is present, those keys replace the URL's embedded credentials as a set. Each key must be a string, else error. Any other type: error 'Expected registry to be a URL string or an object'. A value starting with `$` (`$VAR` or `$VAR/`) is replaced by the env var when it is set and longer than 1 char. token/username/password values of the form `$NAME` ([A-Za-z0-9_]) are expanded from env. An unset variable drops the credential with the warning 'registry <what> references unset variable <b>$X<r>, ignoring credential'. Credentials containing CR/LF/NUL are fatal ('... contains a newline or NUL byte'). Default registry: https://registry.npmjs.org/.

features.name: install.scopes
features.details: Must be an object, else type error. The key is a scope name with or without a leading `@`; an empty key is skipped. The value is the same as install.registry (string or object). It merges into the scoped map that .npmrc already filled; bunfig wins per scope. A scope with an empty URL: its entry is removed, and if it has credentials it is attached to the default registry (the final one after env/--registry, but only when the default registry's own credentials also moved to the new URL, else the configured one).

If the cafile path is still relative after resolution, the install fails with 'HTTPThread: could not find CA file'. Both are passed to the HTTP thread (InitOpts.ca, abs_ca_file_name).

features.details: print: a string. "bun" is a no-op. "yarn" sets save_yarn_lockfile. Any other value errors with 'Invalid lockfile format, only 'yarn' output is implemented' and still sets yarn. save: a bool, sets Do::SAVE_LOCKFILE and FORCE_SAVE_LOCKFILE. path / savePath: strings stored as lockfile_path / save_lockfile_path.

features.name: install.globalDir / install.globalBinDir
features.details: Strings, resolved relative to the bunfig directory, with ~ expansion. Only read from the user's global bunfig (or --config). Global dir resolution order: $BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR > explicit globalDir > $BUN_INSTALL/install/global > ($XDG_CACHE_HOME or $HOME)/.bun/install/global; otherwise the error NoGlobalDirectoryFound. Bin dir order: $BUN_INSTALL_BIN > globalBinDir > $BUN_INSTALL/bin > ($XDG_CACHE_HOME or $HOME)/.bun/bin; otherwise 'Missing global bin directory: try setting $BUN_INSTALL'. A leading ~/ in the env vars is expanded.

features.name: install.cache
features.details: Three forms. Bool: false => disable_cache + disable_manifest_cache; true does nothing. String: the cache directory, resolved relative to the bunfig. Object {disable: bool, disableManifest: bool, dir: string}. Cache dir resolution: $BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR (an empty value counts as unset; ~ is expanded) > configured (bunfig, else .npmrc cache=) > $BUN_INSTALL/install/cache/ > ($XDG_CACHE_HOME|$HOME)/.bun/install/cache/ > the fallback node_modules/.bun-cache. --cache-dir overrides. disable => Enable::CACHE and MANIFEST_CACHE off. disableManifest => MANIFEST_CACHE off.
features.tests: test/cli/install/config-precedence.test.ts ('bunfig install.cache.dir beats project .npmrc cache=', '$BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR starts at the project's root')

features.name: install.security.scanner
features.details: [install.security] must be an object, else the error 'Invalid security config, expected an object'. scanner: a string (a package name or a path). A path from the global bunfig is resolved relative to that file and converted to posix. In the project bunfig, or for a package name, it is kept as is. Setting it disables PREFETCH_RESOLVED_TARBALLS.

features.name: install.minimumReleaseAge
features.details: A number of seconds (must be >= 0 and finite, else 'Expected positive number of seconds for minimumReleaseAge'), or a duration string parsed by parse_seconds: a plain float, or a number followed by s|sec|secs|second|seconds|m|min|mins|minute|minutes|h|hr|hrs|hour|hours|d|day|days|w|week|weeks (optional whitespace before the unit). Any other value errors with 'Expected number of seconds for minimumReleaseAge'. Stored in ms. 0 means no gate (filtered to None at the end of load). --minimum-release-age <N|duration> overrides it.

features.name: install.minimumReleaseAgeExcludes
features.details: An array of strings (a non-string item is a type error; a non-array errors with 'Expected array for minimumReleaseAgeExcludes'; an empty array is ignored). pnpm grammar: `name` exempts every version, `name@1.2.3 || 1.2.4` exempts only those exact versions. A scope's leading @ is skipped when splitting. A malformed entry (`foo@`, `foo@^1`) is dropped with the warning 'ignoring minimumReleaseAgeExcludes entry ...: expected a package name or exact versions'. The CLI flag --minimum-release-age-excludes (repeatable, comma-separated, trimmed) replaces the bunfig list.

features.name: install.publicHoistPattern / install.hoistPattern
features.details: A string or an array of strings (pnpm matcher globs, with `!` for exclude). A non-string item errors with 'Expected a string or an array of strings', which is remapped to InvalidBunfig. Behavior is computed from the mix: AllMatchersInclude, AllMatchersExclude, or HasExcludeAndIncludeMatchers. These are used by the isolated linker.

features.name: install.auto / install.prefer / install.logLevel
features.details: auto (runtime auto-install): true => allow_install, false => disable, or one of the strings "auto"|"force"|"fallback"|"disable"; anything else errors. prefer: "offline"|"latest"|"online", else the error 'Invalid prefer setting, must be one of online or offline'. prefer="offline" also makes `bun install` PreferOffline when no flag asked for more. logLevel: "debug"|"error"|"warn"|"info".

features.name: .npmrc file locations and order
features.details: The user file comes first: $NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG or $npm_config_userconfig (non-empty; relative to the initial cwd) replaces both other candidates. Else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.npmrc, but only if that file exists and XDG is absolute. Else $HOME/.npmrc (HOME must be absolute). Then the project file <top_level_dir>/.npmrc. Later files override earlier ones; npm's config is one flat map, so a key repeated across files collapses to the last one read. An unreadable file is skipped. The global npmrc (prefix/etc/npmrc) is not read. A BOM is converted. Diagnostics: Print, or Discard for runtime auto-install. The header is 'Encountered an error/errors while reading <file>'.

features.name: INI parser semantics (npm/ini compatible)
features.details: Lines are split on \n with a trailing \r stripped. Lines starting with ; or # (after JS trim) are comments. `[section]` headers nest via dots (capped at 512 rope segments); text after `]` makes the line a key. Assigning a section over a non-object key skips that section. `key[]=v` builds arrays, and a plain re-assignment does not clobber an existing array. `__proto__` keys are skipped. A key without `=` is boolean true. `key=` is an empty string. Values "true"/"false"/"null" become bool/null. Quoted values ("..." or '...') are JSON-parsed; on failure, ${} is still expanded. Inline comments start at an unescaped ; or #; `\` escapes. ${VAR} expands from env (the dotenv loader, so .env files count); an undefined ${VAR} is left literal; ${VAR?} expands to empty when undefined. Trimming uses the JS String.prototype.trim set.

features.name: .npmrc keys: registry, @scope:registry
features.details: registry=<url> sets the default registry (declared_in_npmrc=true); embedded credentials are parsed as in bunfig. @scope:registry=<url> sets a scoped registry. Only string values count. Precedence: npmrc < bunfig < env < CLI.

features.name: .npmrc per-URL auth: //host/path/:_authToken|_auth|username|_password|email|certfile|keyfile
features.details: Lines `//<key>:<opt>=<value>` with opt one of _authToken, _auth, username, _password, email, certfile, keyfile. The key is normalized like npm's nerfDart: the scheme removed, the host lowercased, and the default port (443 for https, 80 for http) dropped when a scheme was written. certfile/keyfile warn '<b>certfile<r> is not supported; ignoring this .npmrc option' (no mTLS). Misspelled credential words (case/_/- folded, e.g. `_authtoken`) right after `/:` warn 'ignoring unknown .npmrc option X'. Resolution follows npm hasAuth order per key: _authToken > _auth (sent verbatim as Basic) > username+_password (password base64-decoded leniently, then Basic base64(user:pass)). A later empty value clears an earlier one. An empty _auth for a known registry errors with 'ignoring empty _auth value'. Lookup walks npm's regFromURI: for https://h/a/ it tries h/a/, h:443/a/, h/a, h:443/a, ..., h, h:443. .npmrc credentials only apply over https for package-data URLs (tarballs). A tarball gets the registry's credentials only when it is on the same origin (scheme, host, effective port); otherwise only its own .npmrc line applies. Credentials from bunfig/env/CLI beat .npmrc for the same registry, unless the scope itself came from .npmrc.

features.name: .npmrc keys: cache, dry-run, ca, cafile, omit, include, ignore-scripts, link-workspace-packages, save-exact, provenance, hoist, install-strategy, node-linker, public-hoist-pattern, hoist-pattern
features.details: cache=<path> sets the cache dir (relative to the .npmrc's dir, ~ expanded); cache=false disables the cache. dry-run: "true"/bool. ca: a string or ca[]= array; cafile: a path resolved relative to the .npmrc (ca and cafile replace each other as one setting). omit / include: a string or array with dev|peer|optional; include sets save_*=true, omit sets false. Boolean keys use npm coercion (npmrc_bool): null=false, numbers are !=0, objects are true, strings are false only for empty-after-trim? (empty string => true), 'false'/'null'/'undefined' => false, a numeric string => !!Number, other strings => true. The boolean keys are ignore-scripts, link-workspace-packages, save-exact (=> exact), provenance, hoist. install-strategy: hoisted => Hoisted, linked => Isolated; nested/shallow are TODO and ignored. node-linker: pnpm|isolated => Isolated, node-modules|hoisted => Hoisted. public-hoist-pattern / hoist-pattern: a string or array; an invalid value is silently dropped (log reset).

features.name: Overall precedence: npmrc < bunfig < env < CLI
features.details: (1) The .npmrc files merge (user, then project) into a BunInstall. (2) overlay_bunfig_install puts bunfig on top: the registry replaces; scopes merge per name with bunfig winning; url_auth is appended; ca+cafile are replaced together if bunfig sets either; the other Option fields replace when Some. (3) NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS/npm_config_ignore_scripts (npm bool, non-empty) forces ignore_scripts=true (it can only turn scripts off). (4) Options::load: the registry env vars BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY > NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY > npm_config_registry (trimmed, the first non-empty wins, never falls through) replace the default scope. Credentials carry over when the new URL is the same host and a path prefix, and https is not downgraded. (5) --registry wins over everything and also makes publishConfig.registry ignored. (6) Token env BUN_CONFIG_TOKEN > NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN > npm_config_token sets a Bearer token on the default scope (beats .npmrc and URL-embedded credentials). (7) The other CLI flags last. (8) Finally .npmrc url_auth fills scopes that still lack credentials.
features.tests: test/cli/install/config-precedence.test.ts (~60 cases incl. 'NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY beats registry= in project .npmrc', 'BUN_CONFIG_TOKEN beats the _authToken in ~/.npmrc', '--registry drops the _authToken of the .npmrc registry but keeps BUN_CONFIG_TOKEN')

features.name: Install-related environment variables
features.details: BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY / NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY / npm_config_registry (default registry). BUN_CONFIG_TOKEN / NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN / npm_config_token (Bearer). NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG / npm_config_userconfig (user npmrc path). NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS / npm_config_ignore_scripts. NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE / npm_config_provenance (publish). BUN_INSTALL (root for cache/global/bin). BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR. BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR. BUN_INSTALL_BIN. BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_STORE (truthy => global virtual store). BUN_INSTALL_PROGRESS=0 disables the progress bar (also off in CI per is_ci: CI|TDDIUM|GITHUB_ACTIONS|JENKINS_URL|bamboo.buildKey, and when stderr is not a TTY). BUN_INSTALL_VERBOSE (verbose). BUN_MANIFEST_CACHE: 1 => manifest cache on without cache-control, 2 => with cache-control, other => off. BUN_CONFIG_YARN_LOCKFILE (set => write yarn.lock). BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_COUNT (u16, default 5). BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_BACKOFF (base ms, default 50; 0 => retry immediately). BUN_CONFIG_MAX_HTTP_REQUESTS (1..65535; default 64, also 64 with a proxy; an invalid value errors, 0 warns). BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT (seconds, default 300; auto-install uses 30 unless set). BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_SAVE_LOCKFILE / BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_LOAD_LOCKFILE / BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_INSTALL_PACKAGES (the flag is set to value=='0', i.e. any other value skips). BUN_CONFIG_NO_VERIFY=1|true skips integrity. BUN_CONFIG_MANIFEST_CACHE_CONTROL_TIMESTAMP (debug only). BUN_CONFIG_DNS_TIME_TO_LIVE_SECONDS (default 30). BUN_INSTALL_STREAMING_MIN_SIZE (default 2MiB), BUN_INSTALL_STREAMING_DRAIN_THRESHOLD (256KiB), BUN_INSTALL_WINDOWS_RENAME_RETRY_MS (5000). Feature flags: BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_INSTALL_INDEX, BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_STREAMING_INSTALL, BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_FORCE_WINDOWS_JUNCTIONS, BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_FORCE_WAITER_THREAD, BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_IGNORE_SCRIPTS, BUN_CONFIG_DISABLE_COPY_FILE_RANGE, BUN_CONFIG_DISABLE_ioctl_ficlonerange. BUN_TMPDIR. XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, HOME/USERPROFILE. GITHUB_API_URL (github tarball base, default https://api.github.com). NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED (=='0' disables verification). NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (CA store, handled in root_certs.cpp). HTTP(S)_PROXY / ALL_PROXY / NO_PROXY (see proxy).

features.name: HTTP proxy and NO_PROXY
features.details: The proxy per target scheme: for http URLs http_proxy then HTTP_PROXY; for https URLs https_proxy then HTTPS_PROXY. The lowercase name is checked first; if it is present but empty, the uppercase one is used. Empty-ish values ("", '""', "''") count as unset. The fallback is all_proxy/ALL_PROXY, used only if it has no scheme or an http(s) scheme (SOCKS is ignored). A `DOMAIN\user:pass@proxy` login is supported. has_http_proxy also rejects '0'/'false'. NO_PROXY is no_proxy, else NO_PROXY. Entries are separated by commas or whitespace. `*` matches everything. A domain (example.com, .example.com, *.example.com) matches the name and its subdomains, case-insensitively, with trailing dots stripped. IP literals (v4/v6, bracketed) match exactly, with ::ffff: mapping folded. CIDR (10.0.0.0/8, fd00::/8, ::ffff:10.0.0.0/104) is supported. An optional :port must equal the request port. An IP host never matches a domain suffix. Proxy settings follow redirects (ProxySettings::from_env). A proxy CONNECT failure (407 etc.) is reported with the proxy's status.

features.name: TLS / CA store flags
features.details: --ca <PEM>... and --cafile <path> (replace bunfig/npmrc ca+cafile). --use-system-ca, --use-openssl-ca, --use-bundled-ca: exactly one is allowed, else 'choose exactly one of ...' and exit 1. CAStore values: Bundled (the default: bundled plus OpenSSL default file/dir), System (bundled plus the system's), OpenSSL (only OpenSSL defaults). NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 => System. NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 disables verification for registry requests. Cert errors, ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID and TooManyRedirects are final (never retried).

features.name: Retry, backoff, timeouts
features.details: max_retry_count defaults to 5 (BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_COUNT). A request is retried if it failed with no response (connect/DNS errors) or with status >499, 429 or 408, and the error isn't final (Cert, ALTNAME, TooManyRedirects). Blocking requests (send_with_retries, used for publish-like/sync calls) are not retried after a timeout/ETIMEDOUT or a 501. Backoff: base 50ms (BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_BACKOFF), base<<min(attempt-1,6), capped at base*40, with +/-20% jitter. Retry-After: <seconds> (max 60; the HTTP-date form is ignored) is honored when it exceeds the backoff; it prints 'warn: registry asked to wait Ns before retrying' once per attempt level. The first timeout prints 'warn: registry requests failed, retrying' once per install. Under runtime auto-install the wait is 0. Manifest requests with no waiting dependency are not retried on ConnectionRefused/DNSResolveFailed/etc. A single helper thread wakes the loop at the deadlines. Idle timeout is 300s (BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_IDLE_TIMEOUT); auto-install uses 30s. Concurrency: 64 (--network-concurrency, min 1; BUN_CONFIG_MAX_HTTP_REQUESTS).

features.name: --offline / --prefer-offline / manifest cache
features.details: OfflineMode: Online (default: revalidate stale manifests), PreferOffline (--prefer-offline or bunfig prefer="offline": a cached manifest of any age satisfies resolution; only what is missing is fetched), Offline (--offline or install.offline=true: no network; anything not cached is an error). --offline beats --prefer-offline. In either non-online mode MANIFEST_CACHE is forced on, even with `bun update`, --no-cache or --force. Offline disables tarball prefetch. Manifest freshness: max-age from Cache-Control (no-cache/no-store => 0), capped at 300s (MAX_MANIFEST_AGE). A manifest written with a future clock is treated as expired. Requests send If-None-Match (etag) / If-Modified-Since. Accept is 'application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json; q=1.0, application/json; q=0.8, */*' (corgi). The full document 'application/json, */*' is requested when minimumReleaseAge is set (time field needed). `bun update` never reads the manifest cache. --no-cache disables the manifest cache. --force disables cache-control and forces install and lockfile save.

features.name: Request auth headers and scoped registry selection
features.details: A package name @scope/x uses registries[hash(scope)] only if the stored scope name equals it (hash collisions fall back to the default). Authorization is 'Bearer <token>' if a token is set, else 'Basic <auth>'; it is never sent to non-http(s) URLs. It is accompanied by 'npm-auth-type: legacy'. Tarball credentials: a .npmrc line for the tarball's own URL (https only) or the scope's credentials if same-origin. Unscoped/default-trusted tarball checks compare against <registry>/<name>/-/<name>-<version>.tgz. URL-embedded credential segments in registry paths are recognized and stripped: yarn style '/:_authToken=T', JFrog style '/_auth=<b64>', plus username=/_password=. A trailing misspelled ':<word>=' is stripped and never used.

features.name: Tag inference (Dependency::Tag::infer)
features.details: The input is left-trimmed of ' \t\n\r'. Empty => DistTag 'latest'. A Windows drive letter + separator => Tarball if it ends .tgz/.tar.gz/.tar (case-insensitive), else Folder. Leading = > < ^ * | => Npm. '.' => Tarball/Folder. '~/' => Tarball/Folder, other '~' => Npm. '/' => Tarball/Folder. A digit => Tarball if a tarball suffix; DistTag if it only starts like a version (e.g. 2x, 1beta: semver parse invalid with a wildcard, no |+ or whitespace, not a plain x.y.z); else Npm. 'file:' => Tarball (suffix) or Folder. 'catalog:' => Catalog. 'git://' => Github if github.com/<shorthand>, else hosted-git-info provider tag, else Git. 'git+ssh:' / 'git+file:' / 'git+git:' => Git. 'git+http(s)://' => Github for a github.com shorthand path, else HGI, else Git. 'github:<shorthand>' => Github. 'http:' / 'https:' => Tarball if github.com/<o>/<r>/tarball/... or a .tgz/.tar.gz/.tar suffix; Github if a github.com shorthand path; else an HGI provider; else Tarball. 'ssh:' => Git. 'link:' => Symlink. 'npm:' => infer on the part after the alias @ (or Npm). 'v...' => Tarball, Github shorthand, scp-like => Git, single 'v' => DistTag, v<digit> => Npm unless a dist-tag-like word, else DistTag. 'workspace:' => Workspace. 'x'/'X' alone or 'x.' => Npm. 'patch:' => Npm (patch protocol unsupported). Fallbacks: a tarball suffix => Tarball; a github shorthand (user/repo[#ref], no ':' or '@' before #, one slash, no whitespace before #, not ending in /, not starting with . or /) => Github; scp-like (host:path or user@host:path, no '://') => HGI or Git; no '|' => DistTag; else Npm. Note: gitlab:/bitbucket:/gist:/sourcehut: shortcuts fall to the scp-like branch and resolve as Git via HGI.

features.name: npm semver ranges and dist-tags
features.details: Npm: a single leading 'v' is stripped (vx => x). Parsed with Semver::query::parse (supports =, >, <, >=, <=, ^, ~, x/X/*, hyphen ranges, ||, prerelease). A literal '*' or 'name@*' resolves via find_any_version: 'latest' even if it is a prerelease, unless deprecated, otherwise the highest release. DistTag: the tag defaults to 'latest' when empty. An exact dist-tag name is preferred (find_by_spec). An implicit latest (`bun add pkg`) skips a deprecated latest in favor of the highest non-deprecated version. Deprecated versions are used only if nothing else matches.

features.name: npm: alias protocol
features.details: npm:<name>@<range|tag> is an alias, with scoped names supported (npm:@scope/n@^1). Per Yarn, npm:^1.0.0 and npm:1.0.0 (a range or exact version with no name) are ranges for the dependency's own name. Per npm, npm:x, npm:1, npm:1.x are aliases of packages named x/1/1.x. Nameless aliases (npm:, npm:@1.0.0, npm:@scope/@1) still parse for lockfiles. In package.json they error with 'invalid package name ... in dependency ...' (root/workspace) or warn 'skipping unnamed dependency' (other packages). Only the root/workspace's aliases are registered globally (record_npm_alias). npm:name@tag => DistTag on the real name. A flat override never applies to an npm: alias; only a key spelling the alias does.

features.name: git dependencies (git+ssh, git+https, git://, ssh://, scp-like, gitlab:/bitbucket:)
features.details: Git parse: strip 'git+', split at the LAST '#' into repo and committish. Clone URL candidates (clone_urls): try_ssh (not for http*; git@host:path kept; scp-like host:path => ssh://[git@]host/path, with shorthand hosts github/gitlab/bitbucket/gist/sourcehut mapped to their domain; an ssh:// URL kept) and try_https (http* kept; scp-like => https://host/path; ssh://git@<known-host> => https:// without git@). The last candidate is tried first (https before ssh). Other URLs are passed only if they contain '://'. Process: a bare clone cached by URL ('git clone -c core.longpaths=true --quiet --bare --template= -- <url> <tmp>'), or 'git fetch --quiet --prune --no-recurse-submodules -- <url>' on the cached repo. Resolve commit: 'git log --format=%H -1 --end-of-options <committish>', or for empty/HEAD 'log ... --no-walk=unsorted --ignore-missing refs/remotes/origin/HEAD HEAD'. Checkout: 'ls-tree -r -z' plus 'git -c core.longpaths=true -c core.symlinks=false restore --quiet --source=<sha> --worktree -- .' with GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp>.index into a temp work tree. Every git invocation adds '-c core.hooksPath=<nulldev> -c submodule.recurse=false'. Env: GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1; GIT_ASKPASS=echo unless set or core.askpass is configured; GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -oStrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new' unless GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_SSH/core.sshCommand is set (checked via 'git --git-dir=<nulldev> config --name-only --get-regexp ^core\.(askpass|sshcommand)$'). git is resolved on PATH; if missing: '"git" is not installed (needed for "<name>")'. Concurrency is the thread count; the first task computes the env. After checkout, .git and .bun-tag are removed, node_modules is stripped unless bundled deps exist, and in-checkout symlinks are copied (links leaving the checkout refused). The resolved tag must be a safe component ([A-Za-z0-9._-], <=256, no leading '-'). The lockfile records scp-like as ssh://host:path. #semver:<range> is NOT specially supported: the committish is passed to git log as is.

features.name: GitHub dependencies (github:, user/repo shorthand, https://github.com/u/r)
features.details: Parsed with HostedGitInfo::from_url. A shorthand is prefixed with 'github:'. Owner and project are located in the original text (not the percent-decoded version). The committish comes from a /tree/<ref> path or the '#fragment' (kept as written; control characters reject it). Fetched as a tarball from '<GITHUB_API_URL or https://api.github.com>/repos/<owner>/<repo>/tarball/<committish>' (empty repo => no slash). The resolved tag is '<owner>-<repo>-<sha7>'. Explicit git+https://github.com/... non-shorthand forms become Git (clone) instead. https://github.com/o/r/tarball/<ref> and *.tar.gz URLs are Tarball. codeload.github.com URLs are recognized in lockfiles.

features.name: hosted-git-info port
features.details: A bug-for-bug port of npm hosted-git-info. Known protocols: bitbucket, gist, git+file, git+ftp, git+http, git+https, git+rsync, git+ssh, git, github, gitlab, http, https, sourcehut, ssh. Providers and domains: bitbucket=bitbucket.org, gist=gist.github.com, github=github.com, gitlab=gitlab.com, sourcehut=git.sr.ht (www. is stripped for domain matching). correctProtocol: user@host:path => Unknown; user:pass@host => git+ssh; '//' right after the first colon => Custom protocol; else a split at the colon. correct_url turns the scp ':' into '/' and git+ssh. Default representation: git+ssh/ssh/git+http => sshurl, git+https/https => https, http => http, git+file/ftp/rsync/git => git, shortcuts => shortcut; unknown/custom => sshurl. Per-provider extractors: github accepts /tree/<ref>; bitbucket rejects 'get' paths; gitlab supports nested groups and rejects /-/ and /archive.tar.gz; gist has an optional user and 'raw'; sourcehut rejects 'archive'. user/project/committish are URL-decoded.

features.name: Tarball URLs and local tarballs
features.details: http(s):// => URI::Remote. 'file://' => Local (prefix stripped, 7 chars). 'file:' => Local (5 chars). Any other '://' => error 'invalid or unsupported dependency "..."'. Otherwise a local path. Detection is by suffix only (.tgz/.tar.gz/.tar, case-insensitive, query strings not considered). A package with no name falls back to the basename without .tgz/.tar.gz (URLs drop ?query/#hash), else 'unnamed-package'. In packageExtensions only remote tarballs are allowed.

features.name: file: folders and link:
features.details: Folder: file:<path>. file://../foo and file:///../foo become ../foo (npm compat). Windows /C:/x becomes C:/x. Other 'proto:' errors with 'Unsupported protocol'. Bare relative/absolute paths are Folder. Folder/Symlink paths in root/workspace/folder packages are rewritten relative to the top-level dir. A path escaping is rejected: 'Dependency "x" has an unsafe folder path'. The rule: only the root package.json, a workspace, or a top-level override may link to a path outside (LINK_PATH_RULE); otherwise the folder's lifecycle scripts are not run when it is inside its declarer. A workspace of the same name wins over a file: folder at the root. link:<target>: when the target is a valid package name it is a `bun link` registration (global link dir), else a directory; it is stored in the lockfile with a leading './'. On Windows the paths are converted to posix.

features.name: workspace: protocol
features.details: workspace:*, workspace:^, workspace:~ (and empty) link the workspace of that name regardless of version. workspace:<range> must satisfy the workspace's version, else 'No matching version for workspace dependency "x". Version: "..."'. Ranges that don't name a version (empty, '*', tag-only like `foo@^`) still link. workspace:<name>@<range> uses the alias part as the name. workspace:<path> / workspace:. links by path relative to the package. A workspace: dependency naming the root package resolves to '.' using the root version. Also: a plain npm range on a workspace name links the workspace when link_workspace_packages (default true) and the version satisfies; a dist-tag equal to its own name (e.g. "foo": "latest") links the workspace. Duplicate workspace names error with 'Workspace name "x" already exists' and notes. 'workspaces' can be an array or {packages: [], selfContained: [], catalog, catalogs}. installConfig.hoistingLimits supports 'workspaces' and 'none' only; others warn.

features.name: catalog: protocol
features.details: catalog: or catalog:default => the default catalog; catalog:<name> => a named group. The group name is whitespace-trimmed. Sources, in order: root package.json workspaces.catalog / workspaces.catalogs. If those are absent and a 'workspaces' field exists, top-level catalog / catalogs are allowed. Defining the same dep in both 'catalog' and 'catalogs.default' errors with '"x" is defined in both ...; keep one of them'. Duplicate entries error with 'Duplicate catalog'. An invalid version errors with 'Invalid dependency version'. Only the root and workspaces may use catalog:. In other packages a catalog: dependency is left unresolvable (Uninitialized), and a catalog: peer becomes an optional '*' peer. An override value catalog: resolves through the catalog and warns '<name>@catalog: not in catalog[: catalogs require a "workspaces" field ...]'. `bun add --catalog[=NAME]` writes the entry. `bun update --latest` rewrites catalog entries to 'latest' (keeping npm: prefixes).
features.bun_source: src/install/dependency.rs:1610-1623; src/install/lockfile/CatalogMap.rs (48-100 lookup, 144-180 latest, 209-240 strip_reference, 263-420 parse); src/install/lockfile/Package.rs:3418-3445; src/install/lockfile/OverrideMap.rs:469-501

features.name: overrides / resolutions (OverrideMap)
features.details: Only from the root package.json. 'overrides' (npm) wins; 'resolutions' (yarn) is ignored if overrides exists. A non-object is an error: '"overrides" expects a map of package names to versions'. Keys starting with '//' are comments. An empty key warns 'Missing overridden package name'. Value forms: a string spec (any dependency spec, incl. npm:, catalog:, file:, git), '$name' (uses the root's declared spec for name, or the workspaces' spec if unambiguous; else warns 'Could not resolve "$x": ...'), '-' (warn: removal not supported), 'patch:' (warn: unsupported), empty (warn 'Missing override value'). Nested object (npm): { parent: { '.': v, child: v } } allows one level only (deeper warns 'Bun currently only supports one level of nested "overrides"'). Key selectors: 'name', 'name@range', pnpm 'parent>child' and 'parent@range>child@range', yarn paths 'parent/child', '**/child', '@scope/a/@scope/b', 'name@npm:@scope/other@^1'. More than 2 segments => TooDeep. Bare '@scope' => invalid name. 'name@' => 'Missing version range after'. 'name@npm:^1' reads npm:<range> as a range. Matching: the target range in a key is selected by how the dependent DECLARES it. npm/pnpm overlapping ranges (intersects). The yarn lockfile path uses an exact-text match (lookup_as_yarn). The parent is selected by its installed version (satisfies). Precedence: ranged parent (tier 4) > parent (2) > none, +1 for a matching target range; ties sort by parent range text then target range text; then the flat map. An alias key only selects aliases of the same package. Flat rules don't apply to npm: aliased deps. A top-level flat override of a file: path counts as root-authored (trusted folder).

features.name: packageExtensions
features.details: Root package.json 'packageExtensions' must be an object, else the warning '"packageExtensions" expects an object'. Key: '<name>[@<range>]' (an empty range = all versions; prereleases match too, like yarn). Value: {dependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies, peerDependenciesMeta:{x:{optional:true}}}. Only npm ranges, dist-tags, git, github and remote tarball specifiers are allowed. Bad rules warn 'Ignored "<key>" in "packageExtensions": <problem>'. The first extension for a name wins, but any of them can make a peer optional. Added deps become ordinary lockfile deps. 'Applied' records them (saved in the lockfile) so removing an extension undoes it. pnpm/yarn-berry migration copies pnpm.packageExtensions; yarn berry also has builtin extensions.

features.name: patchedDependencies / bun patch
features.details: Root package.json 'patchedDependencies': {"name@version": "patches/x.patch"}, keyed by hash of 'name@version'. The path is resolved against the project dir. The patch hash (the first 8 bytes of SHA-1) is part of the cache folder name. A missing patch file exits before any linker runs. `bun patch <pkg>` prepares the package for editing; `bun patch --commit <dir>` / `bun patch-commit` writes the patch to --patches-dir (default 'patches'). The patch: protocol inside specifiers/overrides is not supported (warning). Migration copies pnpm/yarn patchedDependencies.

features.name: trustedDependencies (lifecycle script trust)
features.details: The root 'trustedDependencies' must be an array of strings, else error. A declared list (even []) REPLACES the default list. Default list: src/install/default-trusted-dependencies.txt (367 names, max 512); it applies only to npm-resolved packages whose real name (not alias) is listed and whose tarball URL is empty or equals the registry's canonical <registry>/<name>/-/<name>-<ver>.tgz. An explicit list matches resolution.trusted_name(alias, name) and requires an npm resolution or a declaration by the root/workspace. `--trust` adds to trustedDependencies. --ignore-scripts / ignoreScripts / NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS skip all scripts, including root and trusted ones. pnpm onlyBuiltDependencies is migrated.

features.name: minimumReleaseAge resolution algorithm
features.details: A gate is active when ms > 0; it requires the extended manifest (with 'time'). Versions published after (process start - minAge) are 'too recent'. A package excluded by name skips the gate entirely; versions excluded exactly count as stable and win immediately. Range search goes newest first: deprecated versions are skipped (kept as a fallback if not blocked). After a blocked version, an older candidate is accepted if the gap to the previously blocked one >= min(minAge, 7 days) (stability window) or it is older than now-(minAge+7d); otherwise it is remembered as best and the scan continues. Dist-tag: if latest is blocked, older versions <= latest (with the same prerelease tag prefix) are scanned the same way. An exact version that is too recent => TooRecent. All blocked => AllVersionsTooRecent. The result 'FoundWithFilter' reports newest_filtered (latest_is_filtered). Peer warning: 'No version matching "x" found for peer dependency "y" (blocked by minimum-release-age: N seconds)'. `bun audit fix` adds exemptions.

features.name: cpu / os / libc filtering and --cpu/--os/--libc
features.details: Package os/cpu/libc arrays use Negatable: names, '!name' negation, 'any' (= wildcard), 'none' (= unrecognized). [] or absent => all. Unknown positive names => NONE (never matches). combine: added|wildcard minus removed; only removals => ALL & !removed. OS names: aix, darwin, freebsd, linux, openbsd, sunos, win32, android (CURRENT per build target). CPU: arm, arm64, ia32, mips, mipsel, ppc, ppc64, s390, s390x, x32, x64. libc: glibc, musl; libc 0 = not declared = installs everywhere; current is glibc/musl by build on Linux, ALL elsewhere; --libc filters only optional deps (for_dependency). Meta::is_disabled = !arch.match || !os.match || !libc.match; disabled packages are not downloaded or placed (is_row_unplaced), but stay in the lockfile. CLI --cpu/--os/--libc <STR>... accept '*', 'any', 'none', names and !names; an unknown name is fatal: 'invalid <what>: 'x'. valid values: *, any, ... use !name to negate'. Also used by `bun pm prune`-like commands. bun.lock serializes os/cpu/libc arrays in name-map order.

features.name: Peer dependency handling and warnings
features.details: peerDependencies are installed by default (Features.peer_dependencies; --omit peer / install.peer=false / npmrc omit=peer disable them). peerDependenciesMeta {x:{optional:true}} makes the peer optional. Names only in meta synthesize an optional '*' peer (webpack-cli case). A 'bun' peer in a non-root/non-workspace package is forced optional. An unresolvable peer only warns: 'No version matching "<range>" found for peer dependency "<name>" (but package exists)'. A mismatch with the copy the tree provides warns 'incorrect peer dependency "<name>@<ver>": "<dependent>@<ver|root>" requires "<peer>@<range>"' (skipped for optional peers). A peer may also be declared in dependencies (duplicates allowed). Dev/peer priority behavior is tested.

features.name: optionalDependencies failure semantics
features.details: Duplicates between optionalDependencies and dependencies are allowed (the optional row merges). A package is 'required' if any non-optional edge (or a peer served by it that isn't also optional) reaches it (is_package_required). Download/extract errors for optional packages go to on_optional_package_download_error (silently skipped) instead of failing the install. A failed lifecycle script in an optional package deletes it (hoisted: remove_placed_package; isolated: leave_out_entry); --verbose prints 'deleting|skipping optional dependency 'x' due to failed 'script' script'. Platform-mismatched optional deps are skipped. --omit optional / optional=false disables them; required network tasks upgrade an existing optional task to required.

features.name: bundledDependencies / bundleDependencies
features.details: Both spellings are read (bundleDependencies first). true => all deps bundled; an array of names => those deps get Behavior::BUNDLED and are not fetched separately (they come in the parent tarball). This is only checked when the resolver context asks for it (remote packages / manifests via npm.rs). A git checkout keeps node_modules only if the package bundles dependencies. Under runtime auto-install, bundled rows are downloaded lazily.

features.name: Install CLI flags relevant to config
features.details: -c/--config, -y/--yarn, -p/--production (-P/--prod), --no-save (link/unlink default to no save; --save), --ca <STR>..., --cafile, --dry-run, --frozen-lockfile, --cache-dir, --no-cache, --silent, --quiet, --verbose, --no-progress, --no-summary, --no-verify, --offline, --prefer-offline, --ignore-scripts, --trust, -g/--global, --cwd, --env-file..., --no-env-file, --registry, --concurrent-scripts <N>, --network-concurrency <N> (0..65535, stored as max(1,n); an invalid value is fatal), --save-text-lockfile, --omit dev|optional|peer..., --lockfile-only (disables prefetch), --linker isolated|hoisted, --minimum-release-age <N|duration> (fatal if invalid), --minimum-release-age-excludes..., --cpu/--os/--libc..., --use-system-ca/--use-openssl-ca/--use-bundled-ca, --backend clonefile|hardlink|symlink|copyfile (macOS default clonefile, else hardlink), --force. add: -d/-D/--dev, --optional, --peer, --save-prod, -E/--exact, --only-missing, --catalog[=NAME]. update: --latest, -r/--recursive, --depth 0 only.

features.name: publishConfig registry/provenance precedence
features.details: publishConfig.tag/access (public|restricted, invalid => crash) apply unless the CLI set them. publishConfig.registry replaces only the default registry, and only if --registry wasn't given. publishConfig['@scope:registry'] replaces only that scope's. A value that isn't http(s) is fatal. No env expansion; .npmrc credentials apply only over https. Provenance precedence: --provenance (or --provenance-file) / --no-provenance > publishConfig.provenance > NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE/npm_config_provenance (npm bool) > .npmrc provenance. --auth-type legacy|web, --otp, --tolerate-republish.

features.name: Name and path safety checks
features.details: An install folder name must be non-empty, <=511 bytes, each '/'-component <=255 and not ''/'.'/'..', with no '\\' or ':', no ASCII control characters and no UTF-8 C1 controls (C2 80-9F). A lockfile package name additionally may not contain '@' after the first char. Scoped name validity: '@x/y' with the slash not at index 1 and not last. Empty dependency names error with 'empty dependency name (in "<group>")' for root/workspaces. Control characters are escaped in all printed names (escape_control_chars).

areas.notes:
I built this inventory from the Rust sources directly, not the docs. Every path is relative to the repo root submodule/bun. I only explored; nothing was modified.

**Things a port must not get wrong:**
1. **Precedence is layered:** npmrc < bunfig < env < CLI, then a final pass. That pass fills scopes that still have no credentials from `.npmrc` per-URL auth lines.
   - The registry env vars stop at the first non-empty value and never fall through to the next layer.
   - Credentials move to a new registry URL only if the host is the same, the old path is a prefix of the new one, and https is not downgraded.
2. **`.npmrc` mirrors npm's nerfDart / regFromURI key walk.** That includes the default-port variants (`h:443/a/`).
   - `certfile` and `keyfile` (mTLS) are explicitly unsupported and print a warning.
3. **These are not implemented in bun, and they warn or are ignored:**
   - `#semver:` in git specifiers (it is passed to `git log` as a plain committish)
   - the `patch:` protocol
   - `-` (removal) in overrides
   - overrides nested more than one level
   - npm `install-strategy=nested` / `shallow`
4. **The env-var registry is `src/bun_core/env_var.rs`, but it is incomplete for install.** Most install env vars are read ad hoc through the dotenv loader, so `.env` files count. The full list is in the env feature entry above.
5. **Proxy and NO_PROXY live in `src/dotenv`**, not in install. Retry and backoff are in `src/install/retry_timer.rs` plus `download_outcome` in `runTasks.rs`.
6. **Test-only hooks exist.** `bun:internal-for-testing` exposes `load_npmrc` (single file) for unit tests of the npmrc parser.
