features.name: Linker selection: --linker / install.linker / .npmrc node-linker
features.details: Values: "hoisted" | "isolated" (NodeLinker::from_str exact match). Enum also has Auto (default). bunfig `[install] linker` must be a string; otherwise error 'Expected one of "isolated" or "hoisted"'. .npmrc `node-linker` map: pnpm->Isolated, node-modules->Hoisted (yarn spellings), isolated->Isolated, hoisted->Hoisted; unknown values ignored. CLI `--linker <STR>` (install/add/remove/update/dedupe/etc.) overrides config. Explicit value always wins over auto.

features.name: Linker auto-selection (resolve_node_linker)
features.details: If configured != Auto -> configured. Else Isolated iff (configVersion == V1 AND has_workspaces) OR directory `node_modules/.bun` exists in cwd (so a tree previously made with --linker=isolated stays isolated). Otherwise Hoisted. In bun install, has_workspaces = `!load_result.migrated_from_npm() && lockfile.workspace_paths.len() > 0` (npm-migrated workspaces never auto-isolate even if configVersion were 1). LoadResult::node_linker uses workspace_paths from loaded lockfile.
features.tests: test/cli/install/config-version.test.ts ("new monorepos use isolated linker"), test/cli/install/isolated-install.test.ts

features.name: configVersion (ConfigVersion V0/V1)
features.details: Enum V0=0, V1=1, CURRENT=V1. Text parse (`configVersion` key optional): must be an ENumber; 0->V0, 1->V1; non-integer -> invalid; integer > CURRENT -> clamps to CURRENT; negative/other -> error InvalidConfigVersion 'Invalid "configVersion". Expected a number'. Binary lockb: u64 LE after meta; from_int same clamp rule; invalid -> load error. choose_config_version: NotFound/Err -> (CURRENT, changed=true); Ok non-migrated with saved -> (saved, false); migrated from pnpm -> (V1, true); migrated npm/yarn or existing bun lockfile without configVersion -> (V0, true). changed=true forces FORCE_SAVE_LOCKFILE (unless frozen). Written always as second line `"configVersion": N,` in bun.lock. Used by linker auto-selection and security scanner (default V0 if unknown).
features.tests: test/cli/install/config-version.test.ts (new projects use current config version; new monorepos use isolated linker; should add configVersion@v0 to an existing lockfile)

features.name: Isolated store layout (node_modules/.bun)
features.details: Store entries at node_modules/.bun/<storekey>[+<peerhash16hex>]/node_modules/<pkgname>; dependency symlinks inside entry's node_modules named by alias (npm: alias name), pointing to ../../<dep entry>/node_modules/<dep>. Root node_modules/<name> -> .bun/<entry>/node_modules/<name>. Store key: `name@resolution` where name/resolution go through fmt_store_path ('/', '\\', ':', '#', '?' -> '+'); scoped `@scope+pkg@ver`; folder: `name@file+<path>`; root: `name@root` or basename(top_level_dir) if unnamed; git `pkg@git+https+++host+user+repo.git+<commit>`, github `pkg@github+user+repo+<commit>`. Resolution part capped at MAX_RESOLUTION_LEN=80 bytes; longer -> first 63 bytes (cut at UTF-8 char boundary) + '+' + 16-hex wyhash(seed 0) of full resolution text. Tarballs (local/remote) get peer_hash = first 8 bytes (BE u64) of integrity when no peers; with peers: Wyhash11(seed0) over pinned integrity + for each peer: pkg name + resolution string (Posix) -> suffix `+%016x`. URL credentials/query string removed and replaced by hash. Root, workspace packages, link: deps have no store dir (dependents link to their folders). Dedupe: same pkg_id + equal peer set -> share entry; workspace deps distinguished by is_workspace behavior. Re-link: existing entries reused by dir name (package.json not read); `--force` rebuilds all; stale entries remain until `bun prune`.

features.name: Hidden hoist dir node_modules/.bun/node_modules + install.hoist / hoistPattern
features.details: claim_hidden_hoist: a dependency name gets `node_modules/.bun/node_modules/<dep_name>` iff options.hoist (default true) AND (hoist_pattern is None OR hoist_pattern.is_match(dep_name)) AND first claimant for that name (first-wins by BFS order). Name used = dependency alias. Nested `file:` folders (nested_folder) never claim; unlinked members claim too to avoid shadowing. Second alias of a deduped entry can also claim (hidden_hoist_keys). `hoist=false` (bunfig install.hoist bool, .npmrc `hoist`) skips the whole dir and takes precedence over hoistPattern. Only applies to isolated linker. Default hoistPattern is effectively ["*"].

features.name: publicHoistPattern
features.details: bunfig `install.publicHoistPattern` (string or array of strings) / .npmrc `public-hoist-pattern`. Default None/[] (nothing publicly hoisted). Direct deps of root are registered first in public_hoisted so they are never replaced. For transitive deps (including direct deps of workspaces), if not nested folder and pattern matches dep alias and name not yet public-hoisted, the entry is added to root entry's (entry 0) dependencies -> symlinked in root node_modules. First match wins. Packages in global store can't reach these hoists.

features.name: PnpmMatcher pattern semantics
features.details: Input: string or array of strings (non-string array item -> error 'Expected a string'; other types -> 'Expected a string or an array of strings'; in .npmrc an invalid expr resets log and ignores). Each pattern trimmed of whitespace; leading '!' = exclude; '*' alone = MatchAll; else regex `^` + escape_reg_exp_for_package_name_matching(pattern) + `$` (glob '*' -> wildcard), compiled lazily with JSC Yarr on first match; compile failure => never matches. Behavior: all include -> any match true; all exclude -> true unless any match; mixed -> iterate in order, last matching matcher decides (!exclude). Empty matcher list -> false. Port of pnpm config/matcher.

features.name: Global virtual store (install.globalStore / BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_STORE)
features.details: Off by default. bunfig `install.globalStore` bool; env BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_STORE truthy (string_is_truthy) enables, falsy disables (env applied after config). Only isolated linker. Location `<cache_dir>/links/<storepath>-<entryhash16hex>/node_modules/...`; project `node_modules/.bun/<storepath>` becomes a symlink into it. If cache dir path empty -> disabled. Eligible resolution tags: npm, git, github, local tarball, remote tarball. Ineligible: trusted (lockfile has_trusted_dependency or --trust from update requests), patched (name@version in patchedDependencies, or name@version too long), packages with a peer whose `@types/<peer>` (scoped `@types/scope__pkg`) exists in project but the entry doesn't itself depend on that @types pkg; folder/workspace/root/symlink always ineligible; all deps (transitive) of a trusted entry made ineligible; ineligibility propagates up (any dep hash 0 poisons). Hash: Wyhash(seed 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) over [GLOBAL_STORE_LAYOUT=1, no_verify as u8] + store path + NUL + integrity bytes + for each dep (sorted by alias) dep name_hash + dep final hash; result max(1). SCC (Tarjan) members share one hash: each member own=hash_entry(seed0); sub = wyhash(own, per dep: name_hash, in_scc flag, linked hash (own for in-SCC)); sorted, then Wyhash(seed 0x42A7C15F9E3779B9). Concurrency: build under `<entry>.tmp-<random>/`, rename into place; EEXIST loser discards; no completeness sentinel. Entry losing eligibility is detached and rebuilt project-local. Synthesizes implicit '*' optional peer for names only in peerDependenciesMeta. Lifecycle scripts never run inside the shared dir. `bun pm cache rm` deletes links/; `bun pm cache prune` leaves it.

features.name: Materialization backends (--backend)
features.details: --backend values: macOS: clonefile (default), hardlink, symlink, copyfile; other OS: hardlink (default), symlink, copyfile. Isolated uses FileCloner (clonefile), Hardlinker, FileCopier (fallback), Symlinker for dependency links. Stored into global SUPPORTED_METHOD.

features.name: Isolated per-entry task pipeline
features.details: Steps (atomic u32 per entry): LinkPackage -> SymlinkDependencies -> CheckIfBlocked -> SymlinkDependencyBinaries -> RunPreinstall -> Binaries -> RunPostInstallAndPrePostPrepare -> Done; Blocked. LinkPackage: folder deps via link_folder, else link_cached_package. SymlinkDependencies: strategy ExpectExisting when relinking or root/workspace, else ExpectMissing; relink unchanged + not newly trusted -> Done. CheckIfBlocked: block until dependencies finished (cycles not counted); workspaces with scripts (or unfilled scripts) held back while RUN_SCRIPTS so they run after all deps installed. SymlinkDependencyBinaries: link deps' bins into entry's node_modules/.bin, link_to_hidden_node_modules. RunPreinstall: if preinstall exists, task pauses to run it. Binaries: own bins linked after preinstall; commit global store entry. Then remaining scripts. Untrusted non-workspace: blocked script count computed.

features.name: Switching linkers / .old_modules
features.details: Switching hoisted<->isolated reinstalls from scratch. Hoisted install detects `node_modules/.bun` (only when linker explicitly Hoisted and full install) and calls move_node_modules_aside; isolated does analogous. Entries moved to `node_modules/.old_modules-<hex random>` (per workspace `.old_<i>_modules` subdir), entry by entry (node_modules may be mount point). Moved: any non-dot name, `.bin`, `.bun`, `.modules.yaml`, `.package-lock.json`, `.yarn-integrity`, `.yarn-state.yml`, names starting `.pnpm`, prune leftovers. Kept: other dot dirs (.cache, .vite). Scoped `@x` dirs recursed. keep_links (global) skips symlinks. rename fails -> rmdir; EBUSY (mount point) left; EXDEV -> delete_tree; Windows open file -> warn '<err>: failed to remove <path> (installed by another linker)'. Old dir deleted in background after successful install (fail==0). Symlinked node_modules (project or workspace): nothing cleared; warning printed. If nothing moved, old dir rmdir'd. Workspaces outside the project skipped.

features.name: Hoisted install flow
features.details: Lockfile::filter computes trees (respecting workspace filters / install_root_dependencies). Opens or creates node_modules (0o755); fail -> 'could not create the "node_modules" directory'. new node_modules -> skip_delete & skip_verify_installed_version_number; --force or replacing isolated -> verify skipped, delete enabled. Trees installed in iterator order; a tree waits until parent trees complete (can_install_package_for_tree). Packages processed in 16-id batches with run_tasks between. Deferred link batching on non-Windows (up to 64 open dirs). After all: install_available_packages(force), link_remaining_bins, complete_remaining_scripts, wait scripts, link_bins_after_scripts. Self-contained workspaces' trees use copy (copy_trees). Progress nodes download/install/script.

features.name: bin field parsing (bin string/object, directories.bin)
features.details: Bin tags: None, File (bin is non-empty string; link name = unscoped package name), NamedFile (object with exactly 1 string-valued entry), Map (>1 entries, pairs in extern_strings), Dir (directories.bin string, non-empty). Non-string values in bin object skipped (npm normalize-package-bin). `bin` takes precedence: directories.bin used only when bin absent/empty/unusable. Empty string bin -> falls through to directories. Lockfile JSON form: `"bin": "x"` or `{ "name": "path" }` (single-line in packages; multiline in workspaces) and `"binDir": "./bin"`.

features.name: Bin name normalization & target safety
features.details: normalized_bin_name: take substring after last '/', '\\', or ':'; reject '', '.', '..', or names with control chars (skipped). Target rejected if bin_target_escapes_package_dir: first path component contains ':' (Windows drive-relative/ADS), absolute, contains NUL, or '..' climbs above start (CVE-2019-16775). Trailing slash stripped from target. If target has '.'/'..' first component or multiple components, resolved containment check: realpath(package_dir) must be parent of realpath(dirname(target)); on Linux uses openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH first (fallback on ENOSYS/EPERM/EAGAIN/EINVAL). Missing target -> skipped_due_to_missing_bin (no dangling link). Dir tag: iterate dir entries of kind File or SymLink only; missing dir -> skipped. Path too long -> ENAMETOOLONG error.

features.name: .bin link creation (POSIX symlinks), chmod, shebang CRLF fix
features.details: Destination `<node_modules>/.bin/<name>` (global: `<global_bin_path>/<name>`). Relative symlink from dest dir to target. ENOENT -> mkdir -p .bin and retry (not for global). On EEXIST/EPERM/EACCES/EOPNOTSUPP: readlink existing: same target -> ok; different symlink -> unlink and relink (global: only if existing link leads into our node_modules, else EEXIST); regular file/dir (EINVAL): global -> EEXIST; behind symlinked node_modules -> unlink file (pnpm writes files) else error; otherwise delete_tree then relink; ENOENT+writable dir => FS lacks symlinks: warn once '<err>: cannot create symlinks in <dir>, skipping bin links'. After linking: chmod target to 0o777 & ~umask (lchmod) if different. Shebang normalization: if file starts with '#!', >=5 bytes, first line ends with '\r\n', rewrite atomically (tmp file in same dir, preserve mode, rename) removing '\r'. First error recorded, other bins still linked.

features.name: Bin conflict rules (first wins, link order)
features.details: Per node_modules/.bin a `seen` set of destination paths; first linker wins; later package with same name skips (but still chmods its target so `bunx <pkg>` works). Hoisted: per-tree priority queue ordered by LinkOrder (transitive: bool, local_directory: bool, dependency_name) ascending -> direct deps (declared by root/workspace as prod/dev/optional/workspace) before transitive; registry/tarball/git before workspace/file:/link:/root; then alphabetical by dependency name. Global installs: names already present in global bin dir are pre-seeded into `seen` (see_names_in; on Windows strips .bunx/.exe), then link_free_global_bins links remaining global packages' bins skipping taken names. Packages with lifecycle scripts link bins after scripts (bins_after_scripts) in hoisted.

features.name: Windows bin shims (.bunx + .exe)
features.details: Windows: for each bin create `<name>.bunx` (metadata, mode 0o664) and `<name>.exe` (embedded bun_shim_impl executable). If target is directory (EISDIR) ignored. Foreign `<name>.exe` without `.bunx` (global or behind link) -> EEXIST (don't overwrite programs like bun.exe). .exe write EBUSY ignored (shim running). .bunx format: [WSTR bin_path][u16 '"'][u16 0](shebang?)[flags u16]; bin_path relative to parent of shim dir unless is_absolute_target; shebang: [WSTR program][u16 0][WSTR args (trailing space)][u32 bin_path_byte_len][u32 arg_byte_len]. Flags bits: 0 is_node_or_bun, 1 is_node, 2 has_shebang, 3 is_absolute_target, 4.. version (V5=2739). Shebang parse: max 32766+2 bytes; '#!' line (CR stripped); '/usr/bin/env' or '/bin/env' (supports -S) -> program is next token, is_node_or_bun if program is bun/node; else whole line. No shebang -> by extension: .js .mjs .cjs .jsx .ts .cts .mts .tsx .sh -> 'bun run'; .cmd/.bat (case-insensitive) -> 'cmd /c'; .ps1 -> 'powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File'. Shim runtime: node not in PATH -> falls back to bun.exe; errors 'interpreter executable "x" not found in %PATH%' / 'bun is not installed in %PATH%'. Unlinking removes .bunx/.exe pair.

features.name: Isolated .bin linking
features.details: Each store entry's node_modules/.bin gets bins of its dependencies (SymlinkDependencyBinaries) and its own bins (Binaries step, after preinstall). Root/workspace .bin likewise. If node_modules is a symlink (LinkedNodeModules), relative targets computed from real path. Native binlink replacement (see postinstall optimizer) redirects target into platform package entry.

features.name: Lifecycle script names and order
features.details: Lockfile Scripts NAMES (index order): preinstall, install, postinstall, preprepare, prepare, postprepare. Only these are read from package.json `scripts` (string values). Dependencies (npm/tarball/folder/symlink): preinstall, install, postinstall only. Git/GitHub deps and Root: also preprepare, prepare, postprepare. Workspaces: preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare (NOT preprepare/postprepare). Each script run sequentially per package in index order; next spawned after previous exits 0. Root scripts run last (after all deps installed, dep scripts finished, lockfile saved, package.json written), in foreground (stdio inherited, command echoed unless silent), never for global installs, only when install_root_dependencies, skipped on --dry-run. Workspace scripts appended to lockfile.scripts. Isolated: preinstall runs before own bins linked; remaining after.

features.name: node-gyp default script (binding.gyp)
features.details: npm rule wants_default_node_gyp: only when package has no `install` and no `preinstall` script, `binding.gyp` exists in package dir, and package.json `gypfile` is not literally false (unreadable package.json keeps default). Then install slot = 'node-gyp rebuild' (plus postinstall if present; no preinstall). For dependencies only applied when trusted. has_install_script meta set true if any script or default node-gyp applies (root excluded). Registry manifests: hasInstallScript field, or derived from scripts preinstall/install/postinstall non-empty. node-gyp shim: tempdir `<tmp>/node-gyp<random>` holding `node-gyp` (sh: `if [ "x$npm_config_node_gyp" = "x" ]; then bun x --silent node-gyp $@ else "$npm_config_node_gyp" $@ fi`; Android uses #!/system/bin/sh) or `node-gyp.cmd` on Windows; appended to PATH; BUN_WHICH_IGNORE_CWD set to it; removed at exit. Tempdir exists -> crash 'node-gyp tempdir already exists'. JOBS env set to thread count if >2 and not already set (parallel node-gyp).

features.name: Script environment variables
features.details: Base env from `bun run` configuration (loads .env), plus: npm_config_local_prefix = top-level dir (always overwritten); npm_config_user_agent default 'bun/<ver> npm/? node/v<REPORTED_NODEJS_VERSION> <os> <arch>'; npm_execpath default bun self exe if unset; BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_NO_ORPHANS=1 if --no-orphans; INIT_CWD = top_level_dir (no trailing slash on Windows) unless already set; node path: if real node found, load node config; else fake temp `node` -> bun added to PATH (npm_node_execpath). ccache path loaded. Per package: removes inherited npm_package_* and npm_lifecycle_*; sets npm_package_json (abs path), npm_package_name (from list, then package.json name), npm_package_version, npm_package_config_<key> for non-empty string values of `config`. Per script: npm_lifecycle_event=<name>, npm_lifecycle_script=<original script text>. PATH: for each ancestor dir from cwd up: `<dir>/node_modules/.bin`; for dependencies the inherited PATH is inserted after cwd's own chain stops before first ancestor outside store ('/node_modules/.bun/') — untrusted .bin searched last; inherited ancestor .bin entries removed; PATH node_modules/.bin entries realpath'd.

features.name: Script execution (shell, rewrite, stdio, failure handling)
features.details: Unix: system shell found in PATH (`find_shell`) run as `<sh> -c <script>`; Windows or no shell: `<bun> exec --no-env-file <script>`. Script rewritten: `yarn run`->`bun run`; `yarn <cmd>` where cmd not a yarn builtin -> `bun run <cmd>`; `yarn npm`/flags kept; `npm run ` -> `bun run` (with -w/--workspace/--workspaces/--ws/--if-present translated to --filter/--workspaces when no shell metachars); `npx `/`pnpm dlx `/`pnpx ` -> `bun x `; `pnpm run ` -> `bun run `. stdin ignored (inherit for foreground), stdout/stderr buffered unless verbose/foreground (inherit) or silent (ignore); Linux PDEATHSIG SIGKILL. Exit code >0: optional dep -> package removed/left out (verbose warn 'deleting|skipping optional dependency ... due to failed ... script'); else print buffered output to stderr, 'error: <script> script from "<pkg>" exited with <code>', note for git dep prepare ('devDependencies of a git dependency are not installed before its prepare scripts'), remove packages with unfinished scripts (so next install reruns), exit with same code. Signal: 'terminated by <SIG>' then re-raise signal. Spawn error: 'Failed to run <script> script from "<pkg>" due to\n<err>', exit 1. Slow script warning: "<pkg>'s postinstall cost you <dur>" after 30s (5s verbose), disabled by BUN_DISABLE_SLOW_LIFECYCLE_SCRIPT_LOGGING or silent. Verbose: '[Scripts] Finished scripts for "pkg"'.

features.name: Script concurrency
features.details: max_concurrent_lifecycle_scripts default = 2 * thread count; bunfig install.concurrentScripts; CLI --concurrent-scripts <NUM>. Hoisted: a tree's pending scripts can run only after all trees it depends on (its subtree descendants) are completed and alive count < max; complete_remaining_scripts ticks until slot free. Isolated: scripts per entry scheduled when dependencies done (CheckIfBlocked).

features.name: Ignore scripts (--ignore-scripts / install.ignoreScripts / ignore-scripts / NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS)
features.details: Clears Do::RUN_SCRIPTS: no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare for root, workspaces, or trusted deps. Sources: CLI --ignore-scripts, bunfig install.ignoreScripts=true, .npmrc ignore-scripts, env NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS or npm_config_ignore_scripts (npm bool parse; empty ignored; only turns OFF, false/0 can't undo config; not read from .env files). Blocked-script counting still happens.

features.name: trustedDependencies semantics
features.details: Three modes: omitted -> built-in default list (src/install/default-trusted-dependencies.txt, max 512 names), only for Resolution npm and only if pkg real name (not alias) is listed and the tarball URL is empty or equals the expected registry tarball URL for the scope; `[...]` -> ONLY listed (default ignored); `[]` -> none. Name lookup: npm -> real package name, others -> alias (trusted_name). Non-npm (file:, link:, git:, github:, tarball) trustable by name only if declared by root or a workspace with exactly that resolution (can_trust_by_name). `file:` folder inside its declaring package not trusted unless declared by local package or root overrides (is_folder_inside_declarer) -> scripts not run. Root and workspaces always run their own scripts (never blocked); workspace default node-gyp only if trusted. Read from root + every workspace package.json (union). Missing workspace and no list -> uses lockfile-recorded default subset. `--trust` (bun add/install): adds names to package.json trustedDependencies and lockfile; packages reached transitively from trusted update requests also run (only if trustable by name). Lockfile records found trusted names; `[]` recorded explicitly. --frozen-lockfile/bun ci run trusted scripts only for packages they install.

features.name: Blocked script reporting
features.details: For untrusted non-root/non-workspace packages with has_install_script, actual script count computed from installed package.json (with node-gyp default counted). Verbose: 'Blocked <n> scripts for: <alias>@<resolution>'. Summary keyed by name hash, sums counts. End of install: '\n\nBlocked <N> postinstall[s]. Run `bun pm [-g ]untrusted` for details.' `bun pm untrusted` / `bun pm trust` commands list/trust them (pm_trusted_command.rs).

features.name: Postinstall optimizer (nativeDependencies / ignoreScripts arrays)
features.details: Root package.json keys (main package only): `nativeDependencies: string[]` -> NativeBinlink mode; `ignoreScripts: string[]` -> Ignore mode. A present array (even []) disables the respective built-in defaults. Defaults: NativeBinlink for esbuild and @anthropic-ai/claude-code; Ignore for sharp >= 0.33.0 (npm resolution only). NativeBinlink: skip trusted package's lifecycle scripts iff among its resolved optionalDependencies there is one with explicit os AND cpu constraints matching target cpu/os/libc (libc checked for every dep); bins redirected into that platform package (candidates: target path, bin name at root, basename(target) at root, <bin_name>.exe). Fallback when nothing found -> retry without redirect. Env flags: BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_NATIVE_DEPENDENCY_LINKER disables binlink; BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_IGNORE_SCRIPTS disables ignoring. Verbose '[Lifecycle Scripts] ignoring <pkg> lifecycle scripts'.

features.name: bun.lock text format (exact field list and order)
features.details: JSONC-tolerant (parsed with package.json parser: trailing commas). 2-space indent. Top-level keys in order: lockfileVersion (number), configVersion (number), workspaces {"": {name?, dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies, optionalPeers[], unresolved[]}, "<path>": {name, version?, bin|binDir?, ...groups}} (workspaces sorted by path; root always written), trustedDependencies [names] (or [] when explicitly empty), patchedDependencies {"name@ver": "path"}, overrides {name|name@range: value} (scoped rules as nested objects, '.' for flat rule in group; v3), catalog {}, catalogs {name: {}}, packageExtensions {}, packages {"<path>/<name>": [...]}. Package keys sorted by tree depth then path, deps sorted by name; key = relative tree path + '/' + name (root level: just name). Tuples: npm ["name@ver", "<registry url or '' if default registry>", INFO, "integrity"]; folder ["name@file:path", INFO]; symlink ["name@link:path", INFO]; workspace ["name@workspace:path"]; tarball ["name@<url|path>", INFO, "integrity"?]; root ["name@root:", {bin|binDir}]; git ["name@git+repo", INFO, "<resolved .bun-tag>", "integrity"?]; github ["name@github:user/repo", INFO, "resolved", integrity?]. INFO single-line object: dependencies/devDependencies/optionalDependencies/peerDependencies (optional peers only in peerDependencies + optionalPeers list; required peers unresolvable also listed in optionalPeers), unresolved [], bundled: true, os, cpu (Negatable), libc (single name), hasInstallScript: true, bin|binDir. Trailing newline. File mode 0o666 (lockb 0o777). Only tags Root/Npm/Folder/LocalTarball/RemoteTarball/Github/Git/Symlink/Workspace written.

features.name: lockfileVersion versions and stamping
features.details: Text versions: 0, 1 (stop listing workspace deps as trailing object), 2 (strict: off-registry npm tarball must carry supported integrity, integrity supported-or-empty, git .bun-tag must be safe; github tag checked at every version), 3 (scoped overrides objects). CURRENT=3. Parse: missing -> 'Missing lockfile version'; non-integer -> 'Invalid lockfile version'; unknown -> 'Unsupported lockfile version N. This lockfile was likely created by a newer version of Bun. (This is Bun vX, which supports lockfile versions up to 3.)' + note 'Run 'bun upgrade''. Write: loaded version preserved (v0 floored to v1); never re-saved just to bump; scoped overrides + walk-clean -> v3; fresh/v3-loaded walked down to v2, or v1 if any serialized npm pkg lacks supported integrity and URL not under default registry, or unsafe git tag. ParseError list: InvalidLockfileVersion, UnknownLockfileVersion, InvalidConfigVersion, InvalidPatchedDependencies, InvalidWorkspaceObject, InvalidPackagesObject, InvalidPackageKey, InvalidPackageInfo, InvalidSemver, InvalidPackagesTree, InvalidTrustedDependenciesSet, InvalidOverridesObject, InvalidCatalogObject, InvalidCatalogsObject, InvalidDependencyVersion, InvalidPackageResolution, UnexpectedResolution.

features.name: Lockfile load priority and binary/text save format
features.details: Load: bun.lock first, then bun.lockb; non-ENOENT open error -> error; neither -> migrate other lockfile (if allowed). Load error in install: 'failed to <open|read|parse|migrate> lockfile: '<path>'' + 'Ignoring lockfile' (continues unless fail_early/--production -> crash); parse errors don't fail install. save_format: --save-text-lockfile / saveTextLockfile=true -> text; new project -> text unless saveTextLockfile=false -> binary; loaded non-migrated -> same format; migrated -> text unless saveTextLockfile=false. Saving text after loading binary deletes bun.lockb; binary->text conversion saves even if no changes (unless dry-run). Empty lockfile (no packages) is deleted: 'No packages! Deleted empty lockfile' / remove: 'package.json has no dependencies! Deleted empty lockfile'. `[install.lockfile] save=false` disables saving (also force-save flag); `print = "yarn"` / -y/--yarn / BUN_CONFIG_YARN_LOCKFILE writes yarn.lock too. Env BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_SAVE_LOCKFILE / BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_LOAD_LOCKFILE / BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_INSTALL_PACKAGES ('0' means do).

features.name: When the lockfile is saved
features.details: should_save = (!dry_run && binary->text conversion) || (save_lockfile && (meta hash changed / text eql differs || had_any_diffs || update requests || packages_need_update || migrated_from_lockb_v2 || lockfile empty || force_save_lockfile)). force_save_lockfile set by: --force, changed configVersion, migrated lockfile, binary loaded + saveTextLockfile=true, bunfig lockfile.save. Text lockfile changes detected via Lockfile::eql vs pre-clean lockfile; binary via meta hash. Root scripts + package.json write-back happen after save.

features.name: --frozen-lockfile semantics
features.details: Sources: --frozen-lockfile, bunfig install.frozenLockfile=true, --production/-p/-P (also disables devDependencies + fail_early), bun ci. Frozen => save_lockfile=false and force_save=false. Check only if a lockfile was loaded/migrated (NotFound passes). Changed sections: overrides (or 'resolutions' field name used), 'the catalog', 'packageExtensions'; else compare packages: text/migrated/zero meta hash -> Lockfile::eql against loaded (loaded_package_count), binary -> meta hash. On mismatch: 'error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' + 'note: <section> in package.json changed since <bun.lock|bun.lockb|migrated file> was saved[: <first change>]' + 'note: try re-running without --frozen-lockfile and commit the updated lockfile'; exit via crash. Migrated lockfile under frozen: in-memory only, note printed to run bun install & commit. did_meta_hash_change skipped when frozen.

features.name: --lockfile-only
features.details: Resolves and writes lockfile without installing node_modules; disables PREFETCH_RESOLVED_TARBALLS (but still populates cache with manifests and git/tarball deps). Prints log; errors -> crash. Saves even when unchanged (generates meta hash for binary). Skips save if !save_lockfile (frozen/--no-save/--dry-run) unless binary->text conversion. Writes migrated package.json changes then flushes. Summary 'Saved bun.lock (N package[s])'. Available on install/add/remove/update/dedupe.

features.name: --no-save / --dry-run
features.details: --no-save: SAVE_LOCKFILE=false and WRITE_PACKAGE_JSON=false (still installs node_modules). --dry-run (or install.dryRun): removes INSTALL_PACKAGES, WRITE_PACKAGE_JSON, SAVE_LOCKFILE, SAVE_YARN_LOCK; root scripts skipped; no lockfile deletion. Migrated lockfile used in memory only.

features.name: Foreign lockfile migration order and edge cases
features.details: Only when no bun.lock/bun.lockb. Candidates in order: npm-shrinkwrap.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock (v1 & Berry), pnpm-lock.yaml; first that migrates wins; failure warns 'cannot migrate <name> (<err>), trying <next>'. npm lockfileVersion must be 2..4; else 'cannot migrate <f>: unsupported lockfileVersion N, trying <next>' or (install/update/add/remove/link/unlink, not fail_early) '..., resolving from package.json' else error; plus note with upgrade command. pnpm too old -> note 'pnpm install --lockfile-only'. pnpm workspace link to non-existent folder unsupported (warn with issue #23026). 'Failed to parse pnpm-lock.yaml.'. After migration: trustedDependencies read from manifests, root patchedDependencies appended, prints '[ms] migrated lockfile from <name>'. configVersion: pnpm->1, npm/yarn->0. pnpm-workspace.yaml workspaces/catalogs/overrides moved into root package.json on first install (no bun.lock, no workspaces field). Migrated lockfile saved as text (unless saveTextLockfile=false); original kept. Frozen/dry-run/no-save: nothing written.

areas.notes:
I read the sources directly (Rust under submodule/bun/src/install plus the bunfig/ini/install_types crates) and checked them against docs/pm/*.mdx and docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx. I did not run anything. Each test path came from a filename or grep match. I did not open the test files to check their individual assertions, except for listing the test names in test/cli/install/config-version.test.ts.

Edge cases in the code that the docs don't mention:
- Auto-selection also picks isolated whenever `node_modules/.bun` already exists.
- Workspaces from an npm migration never auto-select isolated.
- Workspaces run `prepare` but not `preprepare` or `postprepare`.
- For dependencies, the default `node-gyp rebuild` script only runs if the package is trusted.
- The PATH order puts an untrusted dependency's inherited `.bin` directories last.
- Lifecycle scripts are rewritten so `npm run`, `npx`, `yarn` and `pnpm` calls go through bun.
- The root `package.json` `ignoreScripts` array (postinstall optimizer) is separate from the `install.ignoreScripts` bool. An empty array still turns off the built-in defaults.
- A text lockfile keeps the `lockfileVersion` it was loaded with. A v0 file is written back as v1.
- bun.lock is checked before bun.lockb.
- An empty lockfile is deleted.

Not covered in depth:
- The hoisting algorithm in lockfile/Tree.rs.
- The full binary bun.lockb layout (bun.lockb.rs).
- The internals of the pnpm, yarn and npm migrators.
- Override and catalog parsing.
- prune.rs: removing the older layout and collapsed copies.
- `bun pm trust` / `bun pm untrusted` command output.

Line numbers are approximate and refer to the current checkout.

features.name: Config key [install.security] scanner
features.details: bunfig.toml `[install.security]` table with `scanner = "<pkg-or-path>"`. Must be a string (expect_string error otherwise); `security` must be an object or error 'Invalid security config, expected an object'. Value is an npm package name of the project OR a file path. In the project bunfig a relative path is kept as-is (scanner process cwd = top_level_dir). In a non-project bunfig (e.g. global ~/.bunfig.toml) a non-package path is resolved relative to that bunfig's dir (install_path) and converted to posix separators. is_package_path() decides package vs path. No default (None = no scanning). No env var/CLI override.

features.name: Auto-install disabled when a scanner is configured
features.details: Runtime auto-install (bun run/-i/--install) refuses to install if any of: bun_install config, root bunfig, nearer bunfig, user global .bunfig.toml, or any bunfig.toml from start dir up to project dir has [install.security].scanner. Error 'SecurityScannerConfigured' surfaces as resolve error: `Cannot find package "<x>": auto-install is off because a security scanner is configured. Run "bun install"`. Unparseable config -> 'auto-install is off because a package.json or bunfig.toml cannot be read or parsed'.

features.name: When the scan runs / scan scope (scan_all vs partial)
features.details: Runs after resolution, before linking, for every installing command (install, add, update, remove, patch, link, dedupe, audit fix...). Skipped if --dry-run or Do::INSTALL_PACKAGES is off (e.g. --lockfile-only / BUN_CONFIG_SKIP_INSTALL_PACKAGES). scan_all = update_requests empty OR no bun lockfile loaded (migrated lockfile counts as not loaded; loaded_package_count==0) OR no node_modules dir in root OR subcommand not in {add, install, update}. Partial scan: for each update request, the first importer (root/workspace) dependency that resolves to it is enqueued, plus 'seeds' (packages whose version moved, incl. moved_by_overrides and moved targets after clean): every edge whose target is a seed is enqueued. Then BFS over transitive dependencies with dedupe by PackageID. `bun pm fetch` never scans (verbose note 'packages are not scanned until bun install runs the security scanner').

features.name: Package collection & JSON payload sent to scanner
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-pm-scan.test.ts ('scanner receives every kind of dependency, without the credentials in their URLs'), bun-install-security-provider.test.ts ('handles packages JSON larger than max arg length (>1MB)', 'scanner receives packages resolved from folders and tarballs')

features.name: Scanner subprocess & IPC protocol
features.details: Spawns self exe: `bun --no-install --no-env-file [--use-openssl-ca etc. from Global::ca_store_flag] -e <scanner-entry.ts source>` with __SUPPRESS_ERROR__ replaced by true/false (false only in --verbose) and __SCANNER_MODULE__ replaced (last) by JSON-quoted scanner name. cwd = top_level_dir; stdin/stdout/stderr inherited; env = install's resolved env (no .env reload), plus BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_NO_ORPHANS=1 if parent-death watchdog enabled. fd3 = child->parent result pipe, fd4 = parent->child packages JSON (read until EOF). Child: reads fd4, JSON.parse must be array; `import(scanner)` -> `.scanner`; validates object with string `version`, version must be "1" (else INVALID_VERSION 'Security scanner must be version 1, got version X'), `scan` must be function; awaits scan({packages}); result must be array. Messages: {type:'result',advisories} | {type:'error',code:'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',module} | {type:'error',code:'INVALID_VERSION'|'SCAN_FAILED',message}; exit 0 for result, 1 for error. MODULE_NOT_FOUND printed by child as red 'error: Failed to import security scanner: '<name>'' unless suppressed. Parent waits until exit AND both fds done; drains fd3 after exit (bounded 64 EAGAIN spins). Windows: uv_pipe with non-overlapped child read end.
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-security-provider.test.ts ('the scanner process gets --use-openssl-ca', 'scanner module throws during import', 'scanner missing version field', 'scanner wrong version', 'scanner missing scan', 'scanner scan not a function', 'scanner returns non-array/null/undefined', 'scanner throws exception', 'scanner process exits early')

features.name: Parent-side result validation & error messages
features.details: All via `error: ` prefix (err_generic). No data: 'Security scanner exited with code N without sending data' / 'terminated by signal SIG without sending data' / 'terminated abnormally without sending data'. Invalid JSON: 'Security scanner sent invalid JSON: <err>' + 'Response: <raw>' if <1000 bytes. Not object: 'Security scanner IPC message must be a JSON object'. 'missing 'type' field' / ''type' must be a string' / 'error missing 'code' field' / 'error 'code' must be a string' / 'Unknown security scanner error code: X' / 'Unknown security scanner message type: X'. INVALID_VERSION -> 'Security scanner error: <msg>'; SCAN_FAILED -> 'Security scanner failed: <msg>'. Result: 'result missing 'advisories' field'; 'advisories' field must be an array, got: <tag>'; per item i: 'Security advisory at index i must be an object, got: X', 'missing required 'package' field', ''package' field must be a string', ''package' field cannot be empty', ''description'/'url' field must be a string or null' (missing/null OK), 'missing required 'level' field', ''level' field must be a string', ''level' field must be 'fatal' or 'warn', got: 'X''. Non-zero exit with valid result: 'Security scanner failed with exit code: N'; signal: 'Security scanner was terminated by signal: SIG'. Install wrapper maps errors: SecurityScannerInWorkspace -> 'security scanner cannot be a dependency of a workspace package. It must be a direct dependency of the root package.'; RetryFailed -> '...failed after partial install. This is probably a bug in Bun...'; InvalidPackageID, PartialInstallFailed 'failed to install security scanner package', NoPackagesInstalled, IPCPipeFailed 'failed to create IPC pipe for security scanner', ProcessWatchFailed; else 'security scanner failed: <ErrName>'. All exit 1.
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-security-provider.test.ts (advisory * tests), bun-pm-scan.test.ts ('handles scanner crash', 'handles invalid JSON from scanner', 'handles missing required fields in advisory')

features.name: Scanner not installed: auto partial install & messages
features.details: Scanner must be a root dependency resolving to npm (found by dep name among root deps); if it appears as a dependency of any workspace package -> SecurityScannerInWorkspace error. On MODULE_NOT_FOUND first attempt with root npm dep found: prints yellow 'Attempting to install security scanner from npm...', does partial install of only that package (isolated or hoisted per resolved linker; config_version or lockfile saved_config_version else V0), counts offline misses as failures, then 'Security scanner installed successfully.' (green bold) and retries once. Skips partial install when Do::INSTALL_PACKAGES off. Not a package path: 'Security scanner '<x>' is configured in bunfig.toml but the file could not be found.\n  Please check that the file exists and the path is correct.'; after retry: '... could not be found after installation attempt.'; package not in deps: '... is configured in bunfig.toml but is not installed.\n  To install it, run: bun add --dev <x>'.

features.name: Advisory printing format
features.details: stdout. For each advisory: blank line, then '  FATAL: <pkg>' (red) or '  WARNING: <pkg>' (yellow); if package found in scanned paths: path len>1 -> '    via a › b › <red>pkg</red>' (dim, '›' separator, ancestor names from lockfile; root package name included as first element) else '    (direct dependency)'; package lookup = first lockfile package with that name. Then '    <description>' (multiline control-char escaped) if non-empty, '    <cyan>url</cyan>' if non-empty. Then blank line and summary: '1 advisory (1 fatal)' / '1 advisory (1 warning)' / 'N advisories (F fatal, W warning[s])' / 'N advisories (F fatal)' / 'N advisories (W warning[s])' bold. All untrusted strings pass escape_control_chars.
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-pm-scan.test.ts ('control characters in an advisory are escaped', 'shows correct path for direct/transitive dependencies', 'handles mixed vulnerabilities')

features.name: Fatal abort / warn prompt behavior & exit codes
features.details:
Any fatal -> prints red 'Installation aborted due to fatal security advisories' and exit 1. Only warnings -> prompt: if stdin not a TTY: '
Security warnings found. Cannot prompt for confirmation (no TTY).' + 'Installation cancelled.' (red) exit 1. TTY: '
Security warnings found. Continue anyway? [y/N] '; accepts exactly 'y'/'Y' followed by '
' or '
'; anything else (empty, other text; consumes rest of line) -> '
Installation cancelled.' exit 1; accept -> '
Continuing with installation...

'. Note: CI is not specially detected, only stdin TTY.

features.name: Scanner timing/verbose output
features.details: --verbose (stderr): '[SecurityProvider] Running at '<scanner>'', '[SecurityProvider] top_level_dir: '...'', '[SecurityProvider] original_cwd: '...'', and after: '[SecurityProvider] Completed|Failed with exit code N [Xms]' / 'Terminated by signal S [Xms]' / 'Completed with unknown status [Xms]'. Non-verbose, non-silent, duration >= 1000ms: dim '⏳[<scanner>] Scanning N package(s) took Xms' (hourglass only when stderr ANSI colors).
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-security-provider.test.ts ('shows progress message when scanner takes more than 1 second')

features.name: bun pm scan
features.details: Errors if no scanner: 'error: no security scanner configured' + help text showing [install.security] scanner = "package_name"; exit 1. Prints 'bun pm scan v<ver>' to stderr. Loads lockfile (handle_load_lockfile_errors_for 'scan'; missing lockfile/package.json errors). Always scans ALL packages (perform_security_scan_for_all, runs even if not dry-run check). Failure: 'Could not perform security scan (<ErrName>)' exit 1. Advisories printed; exit 1 if ANY advisory (fatal or warn) else prints green 'No advisories found' exit 0. No prompt.

features.name: bun audit command & flags
features.details: Positionals: none, or 'fix'. 'bun audit fix <extra>' -> 'bun audit fix does not take arguments, it always fixes the whole lockfile' + note; other positional -> 'unknown subcommand "X" for bun audit' + note 'did you mean 'bun audit fix'?'; exit 1. Flags: --json, --audit-level <low|moderate|high|critical> (invalid -> 'invalid `--audit-level` value: 'X'. valid values: low, moderate, high, critical' exit 1), --ignore <id>... (repeatable; matches advisory id exactly OR substring of advisory url, so GHSA IDs work; CVEs don't), -L/--latest (only with fix else '--latest only applies to bun audit fix'), -p/--prod/--production, --omit dev|optional|peer, --dry-run, --cwd, plus shared params. Missing package.json -> 'No package.json was found for directory "<cwd>"' + note 'Run "bun init" to initialize a project' exit 1. Header 'bun audit[ fix] v<ver>\n\n' unless --json/--silent/--no-summary. Reads bun.lock only (no node_modules needed).

features.name: Bulk advisory request
features.details: Packages: lockfile packages with Npm resolution except root; with --prod/--omit filter via reachability from root (bundled included, optional_peer false); grouped by registry scope (scope_for_package_name, compared by url_hash); default registry request always sent (even if empty), other scopes only if non-empty. Body: '{"name":["v1","v2"],...}' (unique versions per name), gzip compressed (libdeflate level 6). POST <registry without trailing slash>/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk with headers accept: application/json, content-type: application/json, content-encoding: gzip, authorization (scope Bearer token / Basic _auth, only for http(s) URLs). Uses registry_request + send_with_retries (retries ok). Responses from multiple registries merged into one JSON object (empty '{}' bodies skipped). Non-default registry failures (status>=400, send error, empty, non-JSON, not-advisories) are non-fatal: those packages counted 'skipped' and warn '<registry> did not answer the audit request (<reason>); skipped a, b' (registry redacted). Default registry failure (or UnsupportedProtocol anywhere) is fatal: 'error: POST <redacted url> - <status|ErrName>' or 'empty audit response from X' / 'X returned a non-JSON audit response' / 'invalid audit response from X: not a list of advisories' -> exit 1. Empty body (incl 204/304) never treated as clean. Response must be object of arrays of objects.

features.name: Audit report output, filtering & exit code
features.details: Advisory fields read: severity (default 'moderate'; unknown severities count as moderate), title (default 'Vulnerability found'), url, vulnerable_versions, id (string or number). --audit-level keeps severity >= level (below_level counted). --ignore counted 'ignored'. No vulns: green 'No vulnerabilities found' + dim '(checked N package(s)[, M below --audit-level=L][, K ignored][, S skipped])' + ' [Xms]', exit 0. Else sorted by package name, per package: red '<name>@v1, v2' heading (installed versions), dependency paths ('  (direct dependency)' or '  workspace:<ws> › a › b <red>pkg</red>'; separator '›' with color, '>' without; BFS over reverse dep tree built from npm packages), each vuln '  <sev>: <title> (<vulnerable_versions>) - <url>' (critical/high red, moderate yellow, low cyan), blank line; summary bold 'N vulnerabilit(y|ies) (X critical, Y high, Z moderate, W low)', then hints '  bun audit fix           upgrade the vulnerable packages within their ranges' and '  bun audit fix --latest  also cross major versions'. exit 1. --json: prints raw merged registry JSON to stdout (unfiltered) + newline; exit 1 if any vuln survives filters, 1 on bad response (raw printed if not NotJson).

features.name: bun audit fix
features.details: Requires lockfile matches package.json (prune::exit_unless_lockfile_matches_package_json 'fix') and writable lockfile: frozen -> 'bun audit fix needs to write bun.lock, but the lockfile is frozen' + note 'run 'bun audit fix' without --frozen-lockfile / --production'; --no-save -> '...but saving the lockfile is disabled' + note. Audits without --prod filter. Plan: upgrade each vulnerable package to lowest non-vulnerable version all dependents allow; exact pins in own package.json/catalog/overrides treated as ^version and rewritten; downgrade only within installed major (minor below 1.0.0) marked '(downgrade)'; '(newer than --minimum-release-age)'; sections 'fixing:', 'blocked by a dependent's range:' (with '(peer)', '(catalog[ name])', '(overrides)', hint '    bun audit fix --latest'), 'no published version fixes:' (hint 'bun audit fix --ignore GHSA-..'), 'not matched to an installed version:'. --latest rewrites own ranges keeping style. --dry-run prints plan only. Installs (summary off), reloads saved lockfile, re-audits; prints 'vulnerable after install:' list, 'Fixed N vulnerabilit(y|ies) in M package(s) (checked C[, S skipped]) [Xms]' / 'Would fix ...' / 'Fixed 0 of N ...', 'R vulnerabilities remaining'. exit = remaining>0. --json single object: fixes, blocked, unfixable, unmatched, unaudited, vulnerableAfterInstall, fixed, remaining, dryRun. Scanner runs on packages being installed.

features.name: Integrity parsing (SRI + shasum)
features.details: Integrity::parse splits on ASCII whitespace and keeps the STRONGEST supported entry (sha512 > sha384 > sha256 > sha1). Entry must be >=7 bytes, '<algo>-<base64>'; '?options' suffix stripped; trailing '=' trimmed; decoded size must be <= digest len; failures -> Unknown. sha1 hex shasum: up to 40 hex chars, even length, [0-9a-f] only else InvalidCharacter. Registry manifest: dist.integrity preferred; if unsupported falls back to dist.shasum silently; if both unusable/malformed (non-empty) -> warning 'Unsupported or malformed integrity hash in registry metadata for <name>@<ver>, tarball will not be verified'; no hash at all -> silent, unverified. Lockfile formatting: SRI '<algo>-<base64>' (max len 95).
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-tarball-integrity.test.ts ('verifies the tarball against the strongest entry of a multi-hash integrity string', 'verifies the tarball when the integrity entry carries an option suffix', 'verifies the tarball against the manifest shasum when there is no integrity field', 'falls back to the manifest shasum ... without warning', 'prints nothing when the manifest advertises no hash at all')

features.name: Tarball integrity verification & --no-verify
features.details: Downloaded tarball bytes (buffered path and streaming path with incremental hasher, hashed before libarchive sees bytes) verified against expected integrity when tag supported and not skip_verify. Failure: log error 'Integrity check failed for tarball: <name>' (for_terminal), Error IntegrityCheckFailed, install fails (no hang). skip_verify = resolution != LocalTarball && !Do::VERIFY_INTEGRITY; VERIFY_INTEGRITY off via --no-verify or env BUN_CONFIG_NO_VERIFY=1|true. Local tarballs (file:*.tgz) always verified. For Github/RemoteTarball/LocalTarball the lockfile integrity = expected if supported (or stays_unpinned) else computed sha512 of the bytes (recorded in bun.lock and in .bun-tag). With --no-verify a .bun-tag never claims an unchecked hash; later install without the flag replaces unverified copy.
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-tarball-integrity.test.ts (--no-verify describe, 'should fail (not hang) when tarball bytes don't match manifest SHA-512', 'should fail integrity check when tarball URL content changes')

features.name: Lockfile integrity validation
features.details: bun.lock integrity strings: empty allowed; unsupported/malformed (e.g. 'md5-...', 'sha512-!!!') -> lockfile version >= 2: error 'Unsupported or malformed integrity hash' (InvalidPackageInfo; normal install then warns 'Ignoring lockfile' and rewrites; --frozen-lockfile exits 1 with no network requests); lockfile version < 2: warning 'Unsupported or malformed integrity hash; ignoring' and treated as none. Tarball/URL deps pin integrity in text lockfile; same tarball via URL and local path produce same hash; lockfile without hash (back-compat) installs and adds hash on re-resolve.

features.name: Tarball extraction path traversal protections
features.details: npm tarballs (npm mode): only regular File entries extracted (dirs/symlinks/hardlinks skipped, like pacote); first path component stripped (depth_to_skip 1; in npm mode a leading '/' counts as an empty first component); any '..' component -> entry skipped entirely (normalize_npm_entry_path returns empty); otherwise normalized. Non-npm (GitHub) tarballs: skip_symlinks=true, interior '..' collapsed; leading '..' rejected. Entries normalizing to empty or '.' skipped. Path longer than max path -> warn 'Skipping entry with a path longer than the maximum path length: <path>'. Windows: absolute normalized paths skipped; in npm mode chars | < > ? : (after drive letter) remapped +0xF000 like node-tar. File modes masked (perm & 0o777) | 0o666 (no setuid/setgid/sticky); dir mode masked & 0o7777 with read->exec bits added (node-tar mode-fix). .bun-tag opened with O_NOFOLLOW. libarchive patched for npm-compat read ('npm' option).

features.name: Symlink target safety (non-npm archive extraction)
features.details: is_symlink_target_safe: absolute or empty targets unsafe; any '..' after a named component unsafe; joins symlink dir + target and normalizes as relative preserving leading '..'; unsafe if result is '..' or starts with '../'. Symlinks deferred and created after files; parent dir stat checked to detect swaps ('Skipping symlink whose parent directory changed during extraction: X'), failure 'Skipping symlink that could not be created: X -> Y'. GitHub tarballs never materialize symlinks.
features.tests: test/cli/install/symlink-path-traversal.test.ts ('should skip symlinks with relative path traversal targets', 'should skip symlinks with absolute path targets', 'should allow safe relative symlinks within the package', 'rejects symlink targets that climb above the package root before re-entering a packages directory', 'does not materialize symlinks from a GitHub tarball')

features.name: Install-target / store write-through protections
features.details: Installer refuses to write/delete through symlinks at node_modules/@scope, node_modules/.bin, a package's own dir, store entries' node_modules/@scope, node_modules/.bun (prune), and links of omitted optional deps; replaces a link where a tarball package should be without touching its target.

features.name: Bin link target escape checks
features.details: bin_target_escapes_package_dir(target): true if first path component (split on / or \\) contains ':' (Windows drive-relative / ADS), absolute, contains NUL, or '..' climbs above start (depth counter). Such entries skipped silently (CVE-2019-16775 class). Applies to bin File/NamedFile/Map/Dir targets. Additional resolved containment check (POSIX): realpath(package_dir) vs realpath(dirname(target)) must not be unrelated (symlinked in-package component pointing outside -> skip, outside file mode untouched); Linux uses openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH) fast path, fallback realpath on ENOSYS/EPERM/EAGAIN/EINVAL. Missing target -> skipped_due_to_missing_bin. Bin names normalized like npm-normalize-package-bin: take part after last / \\ :, '', '.', '..' or control chars -> empty (skipped).
features.tests: test/cli/install/bun-install-native-binlink.test.ts:770-830 ('skips bin entries whose target resolves outside the package directory and keeps outside files untouched')

features.name: Package name / folder name validation
features.details: is_safe_install_folder_name: non-empty, total <= 511, each '/'-component 1..255 bytes and not '.'/'..', no '\\' or ':', no ASCII control, no UTF-8 C1 (C2 80..9F). is_safe_lockfile_package_name additionally forbids '@' after first char. is_scoped_package_name: '' -> error; '@' requires '/' not at index 1 nor last else InvalidPackageName. name_is_single_path_entry (project/workspace/folder names): safe + 0 slashes, or 1 slash with leading '@'. Errors: bun.lock 'invalid package name'; Tree 'Lockfile is malformed (dependency name "X" is not a valid folder name)' crash; package.json 'invalid package name "X" in dependency "Y"' / 'invalid package name "X"' (InvalidPackageJSON); overrides warning 'invalid package name "X"'; manifest URL escaping registry dir: 'invalid package name "X": manifest URL "U" is not on registry "R"' (error if required else warning). pack/publish: name/version must be non-empty strings without '.'/'..' components, '\\', ':' or NUL ('package.json `name` and `version` fields must be non-empty strings'); missing -> 'package.json must have `name` and `version` fields'.

features.name: Registry auth headers & tarball credential scoping
features.details: Scope::authorization_parts: only for http(s) URLs; token -> 'Bearer <token>', else _auth -> 'Basic <auth>' verbatim; adds 'npm-auth-type: legacy' on install requests. Tarballs: Authorization allowed only for registry npm packages (AllowAuthorization); remote URL tarball deps get NoAuthorization from config. tarball_credentials follows npm getAuth: .npmrc per-URL entry (only if https and normalized) else registry creds only if same origin (scheme, host case-insensitive, effective port). Userinfo in tarball URL stripped from URL and sent as Basic base64(percent-decoded user:pass, 'user' -> 'user:'), configured creds win. Scoped registry lookup compares stored scope name (hash collision safe). Credentials containing CR/LF/NUL refused: '<key> contains a newline or NUL byte' (by key name, never value). Embedded URL creds in registry URL path (':_authToken=', '/_auth=', 'username=', '_password=' yarn/JFrog style) parsed and stripped; misspelled trailing ':<word>=' stripped & ignored.

features.name: Secret redaction in output
features.details: redacted_npm_url: replaces URL userinfo (all of it incl. username, except ssh user 'git'; ends at last '@' in authority, authority ends at / ? # whitespace), UUIDs (8-4-4-4-12 hex), npm tokens ('npm_'/'npms_' case-insens + 36..48 alnum) with '***'. redacted_source (config file echo): masks values of _auth, _authToken, email, _password, password, token keys (quoted values or to end of line) with '*' of same length, plus UUIDs, npm secrets, URL userinfo. for_terminal = redact + escape control chars, used for untrusted specifiers. Used in GET error lines, audit errors, scanner payload stripping, publish registry display (href_without_auth).

features.name: Publish auth, OTP, web login & provenance refusal
features.details: Headers: accept */*, accept-encoding gzip,deflate, authorization (origin-scoped), content-type application/json (only with body; verdaccio requires exact), npm-auth-type (legacy if OTP given, else publishConfig/auth-type 'legacy'|'web', default web), npm-otp, npm-command publish, user-agent '<bun UA> <os> <arch> workspaces/<bool>[ ci/<name>]', Connection keep-alive, Host, Content-Length. Missing auth -> 'missing authentication (run `bunx npm login`)'. PUT; on 401: www-authenticate containing 'ipaddress' -> 'login is not allowed from your IP address'; 'otp' -> OTP flow; other -> 'unable to authenticate, need: X'; no header -> OTP if body contains 'one-time pass'. OTP flow: if response JSON has authUrl+doneUrl (doneUrl must be http(s) same origin as registry) shows boxed URL ('press ENTER to open in browser' only if http(s) and escaping unchanged), polls doneUrl (202 -> wait retry-after seconds, default 500ms; 200 -> token (must not break header line)); else prompts 'This operation requires a one-time password.\nEnter OTP: '. --otp flag. Provenance NOT supported: refused with 'X is not supported yet: bun publish cannot generate provenance statements' if --provenance, publishConfig.provenance, NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE/npm_config_provenance env, or .npmrc provenance is true (first source found decides). Also restricted unscoped / private packages refused; tag that is a version/range rejected; prerelease without --tag rejected ('prerelease needs a tag').

features.name: Log levels and flags (--verbose, --silent, --quiet, --no-progress, --no-summary)
features.details: LogLevel enum: Default, Verbose, Silent, Quiet, DefaultNoProgress, VerboseNoProgress. Precedence: --silent > --verbose (or global Output verbose) > --quiet > default. npm aliases: --loglevel=silent->--silent, error/warn->--quiet, notice/http/info accepted no-op, verbose/silly->--verbose, --progress=false->--no-progress. Progress disabled (without_progress) if --no-progress OR env BUN_INSTALL_PROGRESS=0 (any other value of that var forces enabled) OR CI detected OR stderr not a terminal. show_progress only for Default/Verbose. --no-summary or --silent clears Do::SUMMARY (no '+ pkg' lines, no summary, no command header); --silent also sets log level Err. should_print_command_name = !silent && summary. Verbose sets verbose_install (libarchive logs, '[PackageManager] waiting for N tasks', per-manifest '    [Xms]\nDownloaded <name> versions', retry warnings, tarball ' Downloaded <name> tarball').

features.name: Progress bar UI
features.details:
Progress on stderr; refresh_rate 50ms, initial_delay 500ms (nothing drawn before 500ms). Node names: with ANSI colors on stderr emoji prefix: '  🔍 Resolving', '  📦 Installing', '  🔒 Saving lockfile', '  ⚙️  Running script', '  🚚 ' extract; without colors plain 'Resolving
','Installing
','Saving lockfile','Running script
'. Rendering: 'name [completed+1/total] ' or '[n files]' units, chained children separated by '... '; redraws by ESC[<cols>D + ESC[0K; dumb terminal appends newline; Windows console API path. Name truncated at char boundary to buffer. Downloads node total = total_tasks + extracted_count, completed = total_tasks - pending. When progress off but not silent: stderr 'Resolving dependencies' then 'Resolved, downloaded and extracted [N]'; yarn.lock: 'Saving yarn.lock' node or 'Saved yarn.lock'.

features.name: Install summary output
features.details:
stdout. Header (stdout via prettyln) 'bun install v<ver> (<sha>)' / 'bun add v..' / 'bun <subcommand> v..' followed by blank line. Tree: leading '
'; per directly installed dep '+ <name>@<version>' (colors: green '+', bold name, dim '@ver'); if newer version in cache: ' (v<ver> available)'; updates '↑ <name> <from> → <to>' (no color: '^ name from -> to'); workspace sections in --verbose '
<cyan>wsname</cyan>:'. For named add requests: 'installed <name>[@npm:<real>]@<ver>[ with binaries:]' + ' - <bin>' lines; disabled platform: 'skipped <name>@<ver> (unsupported platform)'. Lines: '<N> package(s) installed [Xms]' (bun add: max(success, requests)), 'Removed: N', '- <name>' rows for remove, '<N> package(s) removed [Xms]', no-op: 'Checked <N> install(s) across <M> package(s) (no changes) [Xms]' or 'Done! Checked N package(s) (no changes) [Xms]' when all skipped (bun update with package.json sync: '(up to date, package.json synced)'), failures 'Failed to install <N> package(s)
', fallback '[Xms] done'. Blocked scripts: '

Blocked N postinstall(s). Run `bun pm [-g ]untrusted` for details.
'. Lockfile-only/no-install: '
Saved bun.lock|bun.lockb (N package(s)) [Xms]' or '
Done! Checked N package(s) (no changes) [Xms]'. Timing: integer ms truncated then '[123.00ms]' (bold number, dim brackets) for <=1500ms, else '[1.50s]'. Untrusted names/versions escaped/redacted.

features.name: Warning/error/note message formats & network errors
features.details: Prefixes on stderr: 'error: ' red (err_generic), 'warn: ' yellow, 'note: ' blue, with dim ':'. Errors collected in log printed at end. Manifest HTTP >399: 'GET <redacted url> - <status>' (red error if dependency required, yellow warning if optional). Download failure: '<ErrName> downloading package manifest <name>' / '<ErrName> downloading tarball <name>@<ver>'; verbose retries '... Retry n/max in Xms...' (max from BUN_CONFIG_HTTP_RETRY_COUNT). Also '<err> parsing package manifest for <name>', '<err> extracting tarball from <name>', '<err> cloning repository for <name>', '<err> checking out repository for <name>', 'no commit matching "X" found for "Y" (but repository exists)', 'request failed twice, limiting to N concurrent requests'. Resolution: '<name>@<ver> failed to resolve', 'No version matching "R" found for specifier "S" (but package exists)' / '(blocked by minimum-release-age: N seconds)', peer variants, 'incorrect peer dependency "a@v": "b@v" requires "a@r"'.

features.name: Exit codes
features.details: Global::crash() = exit(1). bun install exits 1 if any_failed_to_install, on InstallFailed/InvalidPackageJSON (log printed), scanner fatal/declined warnings/scanner errors, integrity failures, frozen lockfile violations, invalid flags. bun audit: 0 clean / 1 vulns or bad response; audit fix: remaining>0; bun pm scan: 1 if any advisory or failure else 0. Completions: failure exit code 0 when IS_BUN_AUTO_UPDATE set, else 1.

features.name: bun completions (install shell completions)
features.details:
`bun completions [dir]`. --help/-h prints help. Shell from $SHELL basename: bash, zsh, fish, pwsh/powershell (unsupported: 'PowerShell completions are not yet written for Bun.' + issue link 8939), else 'Unknown or unsupported shell. Please set $SHELL to one of zsh, fish, or bash.' + note 'To manually output completions, run 'bun getcompletes''. If stdout not a TTY (and not auto-update): writes embedded script to stdout (EPIPE ignored), exit 0. Also creates bunx symlink next to bun exe (or in $BUN_INSTALL/bin, ~/.bun/bin, ~/.local/bin); Windows: bunx.cmd ('@%~dp0bun.exe x %*') / uninstall.ps1 if in bun\bin. Filenames: fish 'bun.fish', zsh '_bun', bash 'bun.completion.bash'. Dir: explicit arg (relative resolved vs cwd; must be accessible) else search: fish: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/fish/completions, $XDG_DATA_HOME/fish/completions, ~/.config/fish/completions, macOS /opt/homebrew|/usr/local/share/fish/completions, /etc/fish/completions; zsh: each $fpath entry, $XDG_DATA_HOME/zsh-completions, $BUN_INSTALL, ~/.oh-my-zsh/completions, ~/.bun, /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions, /usr/local/share/zsh/completions, /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/{completions,site-functions}; bash: $XDG_DATA_HOME|$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bash-completion/completions, ~/.oh-my-bash/custom/completions, ~/.bash_completion.d, /opt/homebrew|/opt/local share bash-completion. None: 'error: Could not find a directory to install completions in.' + zsh tip + pipe hint. zsh: appends '
# bun completions
[ -s "<path>" ] && source "<path>"
' to $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc, ~/.zshrc or ~/.zshenv unless already contains path / '# bun completions' / '/.bun/_bun' ('Enabled loading bun's completions in .zshrc'); else prints instruction. Success 'Installed completions to <dir>/<file>'.

features.name: bun getcompletes (dynamic completion backend) & completion scripts
features.details: `bun getcompletes [filter] [prefix]`. No filter: scripts+bins+files plus default command list (build install add run update link unlink remove create bun upgrade discord test pm x repl info); reject list same plus completions/help. Filters: s=scripts, i=ScriptExclude + default list, b=bins, r=All, g=AllPlusBunJs, j=BunJs files, z=scripts with descriptions (tab separated), a <prefix>=npm package names from embedded zstd-compressed list (add_completions.txt ~10k names, per-letter index, BIGGEST_LIST 1034) filtered by prefix (first letter must be a-z). Output delimiter: ' ' for fish (SHELL=fish), '\n' otherwise; descriptions appended '\t<desc>' (note: loop indexes descriptions[i] instead of i+1 — off-by-one after first item). Static scripts completions/bun.bash, bun.zsh, bun.fish (call 'bun getcompletes s/i/b/j/z/a'), embedded zstd-compressed in release; completions/bun-cli.json metadata generated by misctools/generate-cli-completions.ts; add list by misctools/generate-add-completions.ts.

Things to replicate or fix deliberately:
- The scanner warn prompt checks only whether stdin is a TTY. The docs say "in CI, exits immediately", but the code has no separate CI check.
- `bun pm scan` exits 1 when there are only warnings, and it never prompts.
- In the security advisory "via" path, the root package's name comes first, because pkg_path[0] is the importer.
- An advisory is matched to the first lockfile package with that name, so a name with several versions may show the wrong path.
- shell_completions.rs print() has an off-by-one: it indexes descriptions[i] for commands[1..].
- Timing format truncates to whole ms and then prints with 2 decimals, giving "[123.00ms]". Above 1500ms it switches to seconds, e.g. "[1.50s]".
- Audit treats unknown severities as moderate.

I covered `bun audit fix` at summary level. The details of its fix-planning algorithm are in src/install/audit_fix.rs (about 1400 lines) and docs/pm/cli/audit.mdx.

features.name: package.json "workspaces" field parsing and member discovery
features.details: "workspaces" can be an array of globs, or an object whose "packages" key is an array. Any other shape means no workspaces. Full glob syntax is supported, including negative patterns ('!**/excluded/**'). A negative pattern removes matches no matter where it sits in the list, and '!dir/**' removes dir itself plus everything below it. A negative pattern does NOT remove a directory that is listed by its literal path. A matched package.json with a missing or empty "name" is skipped: it is not linked into node_modules and its deps are not installed. If that skipped package.json declares dependencies, the warning 'skipping workspace "<dir>": package.json has no "name"' is printed. Workspaces may live outside the root dir (e.g. "../shared" or a symlink). Such external workspaces are installed, recorded in bun.lock and have their scripts run, but bun prune never cleans their node_modules and a linker switch never moves them aside. Workspace names are sorted for determinism. `workspace:*` on the root package's own name links the root. bun run --filter and --workspaces honour the same exclusions.

features.name: Self-contained workspaces (installConfig.hoistingLimits / workspaces.selfContained)
features.details: There are two ways to mark a workspace. One is per-workspace, in its own package.json: "installConfig": {"hoistingLimits": "workspaces"} (Yarn key, and only the value "workspaces" changes layout; "none" is accepted, any other value is kept and warned about). The other is in the root package.json: "workspaces": {"packages": [...], "selfContained": ["apps/desktop"]}, where entries are workspace relative paths or package names; entries that match no workspace get a warning. Effect with the hoisted linker: the workspace acts as a hoisting barrier, so none of its direct or transitive deps (including those reached through other workspaces it depends on) are placed above <ws>/node_modules. Its packages are materialized as real copies, not hardlinks or clones from the cache. The setting is NOT recorded in the lockfile and is re-read from package.json on every install, --frozen-lockfile included, so the lockfile is identical with or without it. It has no effect with the isolated linker.

features.name: bun install --filter (partial workspace installs)
features.details: `bun install --filter <pattern>` (repeatable, supports '!' negation, name globs and './path' globs, same grammar as run --filter) installs dependencies for the matching workspaces only. Example: --filter 'pkg-*' --filter '!pkg-c'. Only the selected importers' dependencies are linked (LinkTargets; None means root). Patterns that match nothing are reported (unmatched_patterns). --filter cannot be combined with --global (error '--filter cannot be used with --global'). The existing inventory only covers --filter for add/remove/update/outdated/run.

features.name: --only-missing (add)
features.details: `bun add --only-missing` only writes a dependency to package.json if it is not already present in any dependency group. Existing entries are left untouched, including their range. The flag sets Enable::only_missing, and the PackageJSONEditor checks it (only_add_missing) while it edits dependency lists. The flag is listed in the add/install param tables.

features.name: --network-concurrency <NUM>
features.details: This sets the maximum number of simultaneous HTTP requests (default 64). It is parsed as u16 base 10. On a parse failure it prints 'Expected --network-concurrency to be a number between 0 and 65535: <v>' and crashes (exit 1). The value is clamped to at least 1 (max(1)) and stored in http::async_http::MAX_SIMULTANEOUS_REQUESTS. It is part of the shared install/add/remove/update flag table.

features.name: Registry manifest request headers and on-disk manifest cache (freshness, ETag, Cache-Control)
features.details: Accept header: abbreviated manifests use 'application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json; q=1.0, application/json; q=0.8, */*'. This deliberately loose value works around JFrog RTFACT-18398 / bun#341. When the full document is needed, the Accept is 'application/json, */*' (needs_extended, e.g. minimumReleaseAge 'time' data, or npm::name_suggests_libc(name) for libc filtering). Conditional requests send If-None-Match (etag, stored when < 64 bytes) and If-Modified-Since (last-modified). A 304 reuses the cached manifest; a 304 with no cached manifest is UnexpectedNotModified. Status mapping: 400 -> BadRequest, 429 -> TooManyRequests, 404 -> NotFound, 5xx -> HTTPInternalServerError. Freshness: MAX_MANIFEST_AGE = 300 s is the default and also the upper bound. Cache-Control max-age=N lowers it (min), and no-cache or no-store sets it to 0. The Age header is ignored. A cached manifest whose expiry is later than now + 300 s (clock skew) counts as expired. On-disk format is binary, at <cache>/<hash(name)>.npm (flat, hash avoids scoped dirs). --force refetches ranges/tags but not versions already in bun.lock or exact versions found in the cached manifest. bun update never reads the manifest cache.

features.name: Global cache directory entry naming scheme
features.details: npm packages from the default registry are stored as '<name>@<major>.<minor>.<patch>[-<pre hash 16 lower hex>][+<build hash 16 UPPER hex>]@@@<CacheVersion>[_patch_hash=<hex>]'. Prerelease and build tags are replaced by a hash to keep paths short. CacheVersion::CURRENT = 1. Packages from non-default scopes or registries (or when the default scope was overridden) get '<name>@<ver>[...]@@<hostname>[__<16 hex hash of href>]@@@1[_patch_hash=..]'. The hostname is truncated to 12 chars if it is longer than 32 or if buffer space is under 64. The '__hash' suffix is added when the host was truncated, the scheme is not https, a port is present, or the pathname is longer than '/'. Git deps use '@G@<resolved>[_patch_hash=..]' (or '@G@<committish>@@@1' when unresolved). GitHub deps use '@GH@<resolved>@@@1[_patch_hash]' (guess form '@GH@<owner>-<repo>-<committish>@@@1'). Default cache root is ~/.bun/install/cache (BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR). The global store lives at <cache>/links/. bun pm cache rm deletes both.

features.name: node_modules up-to-date fast path / cache reuse check
features.details: Before installing, if node_modules exists, bun checks that every expected package is present with a compatible version. If all are, install completes without work. The hoisted linker reads "name" and "version" from each installed package.json. The isolated linker only checks that the store entry exists. If a package is missing or incompatible, bun looks for a compatible version in the cache (any cached version satisfying the range, so no re-download) and installs from it. Otherwise it downloads.

features.name: bun update -g / --global
features.details: `bun update -g` updates the packages that were installed with `bun add -g`, all of them or the named ones (e.g. `bun update -g typescript`). It operates on the global dir's package.json and lockfile. Note that --catalog and --filter are rejected together with --global.

features.name: bun ./bun.lockb [--hash] (print binary lockfile)
features.details: When the AutoCommand has exactly one entry point with the extension .lockb, bun prints that binary lockfile in yarn.lock v1 format (lockfile::Printer, Yarn printer). If argv contains '--hash', it instead opens the file and prints its lockfile hash (PackageManagerCommand::print_hash). An open failure prints 'failed to open lockfile' and crashes. The '--hash' entry in the pm param table exists for this path.

features.name: link/unlink inverted --save default
features.details: bun link and bun unlink use LINK_SHARED_PARAMS: '--no-save' is the default and '--save' is opt-in ('Update package.json and save a lockfile (false by default)'). Every other install command saves by default ('--save (true by default)').
